summary.en: In two campaigns Emperor Trajan defeated King Decebalus and annexed Dacia north of the Danube. Apollodorus of Damascus bridged the river at Drobeta, the gold of Dacia paid for Trajan's Forum in Rome, and Trajan's Column recorded the war in a spiral relief.
summary.zh: 图拉真皇帝两次出征，击败国王德凯巴卢斯，吞并多瑙河以北的达契亚。大马士革的阿波罗多洛斯在德罗贝塔架起多瑙河大桥，达契亚的黄金为罗马图拉真广场提供了财源，图拉真纪功柱以螺旋浮雕记录了这场战争。

label.zh: 大军在辛吉杜努姆附近集结
在莱德拉塔渡河
塔佩之战
德罗贝塔大桥
萨尔米泽杰图萨陷落

sources.title: Ian Haynes & W. S. Hanson (eds.), Roman Dacia (2004)

name.zh: 斯普利特的戴克里先宫

summary.en: Emperor Diocletian built a fortified retirement palace on the Dalmatian coast near his birthplace Salona and lived there after abdicating in 305. After the Avar–Slav sack of Salona in the 7th century refugees moved inside its walls, and the palace grew into the city of Split.
summary.zh: 戴克里先皇帝在其出生地萨罗纳附近的达尔马提亚海岸修建了一座设防的退休宫殿，305年退位后居住于此。7世纪阿瓦尔人和斯拉夫人洗劫萨罗纳后，难民迁入宫墙之内，宫殿逐渐发展为斯普利特城。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage: Historical Complex of Split with the Palace of Diocletian

note: Construction dates are approximate (c. 295–305).

name.zh: 乌尔菲拉的哥特文圣经

summary.en: The Gothic bishop Wulfila, who led his Christian followers across the Danube into Moesia around 348, devised a Gothic alphabet and translated most of the Bible into Gothic. It is the oldest substantial text in any Germanic language and spread Arian Christianity among the Goths.
summary.zh: 哥特主教乌尔菲拉约348年率信徒渡过多瑙河迁入默西亚，他创制哥特字母并把圣经大部分译成哥特语。这是现存最古老的大篇幅日耳曼语文献，也使阿里乌派基督教在哥特人中传播开来。

sources.title: Peter Heather & John Matthews, The Goths in the Fourth Century (1991)

note: Dates of the translation are approximate; Wulfila worked near Nicopolis ad Istrum (northern Bulgaria), used here as the location.

name.zh: 君士坦丁堡的狄奥多西城墙

summary.en: Under the regent Anthemius in the reign of Theodosius II, Constantinople was enclosed by a new land wall some 6 km long, later doubled with an outer wall and moat. The triple line protected the capital for a thousand years until the Ottoman cannon of 1453.
summary.zh: 在狄奥多西二世时期摄政安提米乌斯主持下，君士坦丁堡修建了长约6公里的新陆墙，后又加筑外墙与护城壕。这道三重防线保护帝都长达千年，直到1453年奥斯曼人的巨炮。

sources.title: Stephen R. Turnbull, The Walls of Constantinople AD 324–1453 (2004)

summary.en: A commission led by Tribonian compiled Justinian's Code, the Digest of classical jurists and the Institutes, a student textbook. Rediscovered in 11th-century Italy and taught at Bologna, the collection became the foundation of civil law in most of continental Europe and beyond.
summary.zh: 特里波尼安领导的委员会编纂了《查士丁尼法典》、汇集古典法学家论述的《学说汇纂》以及供学生使用的《法学阶梯》。这部法律汇编11世纪在意大利被重新发现、在博洛尼亚得到讲授，成为欧洲大陆乃至更广地区大陆法系的基础。

sources.title: Caroline Humfress, "Law and Legal Practice in the Age of Justinian", in M. Maas (ed.), The Cambridge Companion to the Age of Justinian (2005)

story.en:
When Justinian came to the throne in 527, Roman law was a thicket of conflicting imperial rulings and the writings of long-dead jurists. Within months he appointed a commission, and in 529 the first Code was issued. In 530 the jurist Tribonian was set to a far larger task: reading some two thousand books of classical legal opinion and condensing them into fifty books, the Digest, published in 533 together with the Institutes for students.

A revised Code followed in 534, and Justinian's later laws, the Novels, were mostly issued in Greek, the language of his subjects. In the West the collection was nearly forgotten until a manuscript of the Digest surfaced in Italy and teachers at Bologna began lecturing on it around 1100. From there "the civil law" spread into the universities and courts of Europe, and its concepts still shape the legal codes of countries from France to Japan.
story.zh:
527年查士丁尼即位时，罗马法是一堆相互矛盾的皇帝敕令和早已作古的法学家著作。他在数月内组建委员会，529年颁布第一部法典。530年，法学家特里波尼安受命承担更艰巨的任务：通读约两千卷古典法学著作，将其浓缩为五十卷的《学说汇纂》，于533年与供学生使用的《法学阶梯》一同颁布。

534年颁布修订版法典，查士丁尼此后的新法（《新律》）多以臣民所用的希腊语发布。在西方，这部汇编几乎被遗忘，直到《学说汇纂》的一部抄本在意大利重现，约1100年博洛尼亚的教师开始讲授它。“市民法”由此进入欧洲的大学和法庭，其概念至今仍影响着从法国到日本的法典。

summary.en: Rival chariot-racing factions, the Blues and the Greens, united against Justinian's government and burned much of central Constantinople, including the old Hagia Sophia. Encouraged by Empress Theodora, Justinian stayed; Belisarius and Mundus trapped the rioters in the Hippodrome and killed tens of thousands.
summary.zh: 战车竞技的对立派别蓝党与绿党联合反抗查士丁尼政府，焚毁君士坦丁堡市中心大片区域，包括旧圣索菲亚教堂。在皇后狄奥多拉的鼓励下，查士丁尼没有出逃；贝利撒留和蒙杜斯将暴民围困在竞技场内，杀死数万人。

sources.title: Procopius, History of the Wars I.24
Geoffrey Greatrex, "The Nika Riot: A Reappraisal", Journal of Hellenic Studies 117 (1997)

note: The death toll (Procopius gives about 30,000) is a contemporary estimate.

story.en:
The races in the Hippodrome were Constantinople's great political theatre, and the Blue and Green factions behaved like street parties. In January 532, after the city prefect hanged some rioters and two condemned men, one Blue and one Green, survived the gallows, the factions united under the cry "Nika!" ("Conquer!"). For five days they burned the city centre, demanded the dismissal of hated ministers and finally crowned a rival emperor, Hypatius.

Procopius says Justinian's ships were ready for flight when Theodora rose in council and declared that royalty was a fine burial shroud. Whatever her exact words, the emperor stayed. Belisarius and Mundus led their troops into the packed Hippodrome from two sides; Procopius puts the dead at about 30,000. Hypatius was executed, and within weeks Justinian began rebuilding on the ashes, starting with a new, far grander Hagia Sophia.
story.zh:
竞技场里的战车比赛是君士坦丁堡最重要的政治舞台，蓝、绿两派俨然街头政党。532年1月，城市长官绞死几名闹事者，其中一名蓝党和一名绿党死囚侥幸未死，两派于是在“尼卡！”（“胜利！”）的呼声中联合起来。他们连续五天焚烧市中心，要求罢免遭人憎恨的大臣，最后拥立许帕提乌斯为皇帝。

据普罗科匹厄斯记载，查士丁尼的船只已备好出逃，狄奥多拉却在御前会议上起身说，帝王的紫袍是最好的裹尸布。无论原话如何，皇帝留了下来。贝利撒留和蒙杜斯率兵从两侧冲进挤满人群的竞技场，普罗科匹厄斯称死者约三万。许帕提乌斯被处死；数周之内，查士丁尼便在废墟上重建，首先就是一座更为宏伟的新圣索菲亚大教堂。

summary.en: After taking Vandal Africa in 533–534, Justinian sent Belisarius against the Ostrogothic kingdom of Italy. Sicily, Naples, Rome and Ravenna fell by 540, but King Totila fought back, and only Narses's victories of 552–554 ended the war, leaving Italy devastated.
summary.zh: 533—534年夺取汪达尔人的北非后，查士丁尼派贝利撒留进攻意大利的东哥特王国。至540年西西里、那不勒斯、罗马和拉文纳相继陷落，但国王托提拉卷土重来，直到纳尔西斯在552—554年连战连捷，战争才告结束，意大利已残破不堪。

label.zh: 贝利撒留攻取迦太基（汪达尔战争）
占领西西里
围攻并攻克那不勒斯
贝利撒留坚守罗马抵御维蒂吉斯
拉文纳投降
托提拉夺回罗马
纳尔西斯在塔吉内击败托提拉

label.en: Narses defeats the Franks at Casilinum
label.zh: 纳尔西斯在卡西利努姆击败法兰克人

sources.title: Procopius, History of the Wars, Books V–VIII
Britannica: Justinian I: Reconquest of the West
J. A. S. Evans, The Age of Justinian (1996)

story.en:
Justinian believed the lost western provinces were still Roman by right. The Vandal kingdom fell to Belisarius with startling speed in 533–534, and in 535 the general landed in Sicily. Naples fell when his soldiers crept through a disused aqueduct, and in 537–538 he held Rome for a year against the Gothic king Witiges. In 540 Ravenna opened its gates after the Goths offered to make Belisarius their own emperor, a ruse he accepted and then betrayed.

The victory did not last. Plague struck in 541, Persia attacked in the east, and the new Gothic king Totila won back almost all of Italy, taking Rome twice. Only in 552 did the aged eunuch Narses, with a large army, kill Totila at Taginae. Italy emerged ruined, its cities emptied, and within fourteen years of the peace the Lombards overran most of it.
story.zh:
查士丁尼认为失去的西部行省依然理当属于罗马。533—534年，汪达尔王国以惊人的速度败于贝利撒留之手；535年，这位将军登陆西西里。他的士兵沿一条废弃的引水渠潜入城中，攻下那不勒斯；537—538年，他在罗马坚守一年，抵挡哥特国王维蒂吉斯。540年，哥特人提出拥立贝利撒留为他们的皇帝，他假意接受，拉文纳随即开城，他却背弃了承诺。

胜利并不长久。541年瘟疫爆发，波斯在东方进攻，新任哥特国王托提拉几乎收复整个意大利，两度攻占罗马。直到552年，年迈的宦官将领纳尔西斯率大军在塔吉内击杀托提拉。意大利从战争中走出时已满目疮痍，城市凋敝；和平后不到十四年，伦巴第人便占领了其大部分地区。

name.zh: 阿瓦尔—波斯围攻君士坦丁堡

summary.en: While Emperor Heraclius campaigned deep in the Caucasus, the Avar khagan and his Slav allies besieged Constantinople from the west as a Persian army waited across the Bosporus. The city held under the patrician Bonus and Patriarch Sergius, and the destruction of the Slav canoe fleet ended the siege.
summary.zh: 皇帝希拉克略深入高加索作战之际，阿瓦尔可汗率斯拉夫盟军从西面围攻君士坦丁堡，一支波斯军队则在博斯普鲁斯海峡对岸等待会师。城市在贵族波努斯和牧首塞尔吉乌斯指挥下坚守，斯拉夫独木舟船队覆灭后，围城宣告失败。

sources.title: James Howard-Johnston, Witnesses to a World Crisis (2010)

name.zh: 阿拉伯人围攻君士坦丁堡（717—718年）

summary.en: An Umayyad army and fleet under Maslama ibn Abd al-Malik besieged Constantinople by land and sea. Emperor Leo III's Greek fire, a severe winter, famine and Bulgar attacks destroyed the besiegers, and the failure halted the Arab advance into south-eastern Europe.
summary.zh: 倭马亚王朝将领马斯拉马·伊本·阿卜杜勒·马利克率陆海军围攻君士坦丁堡。利奥三世的希腊火、严冬、饥荒和保加尔人的攻击摧毁了围城大军，这次失败遏止了阿拉伯人向东南欧的推进。

sources.title: Marek Jankowiak, "The First Arab Siege of Constantinople", Travaux et Mémoires 17 (2013)

story.en:
In the summer of 717 the Umayyad prince Maslama crossed the Hellespont with an army the chroniclers counted in the hundreds of thousands, dug a ditch around the land walls and waited for a great fleet. Leo III, crowned only that March, held a city already stocked with grain for a long siege. As the Arab fleet sailed past the city into the Bosporus, a Byzantine squadron attacked its rearguard with Greek fire, the secret incendiary that burned even on water.

The winter that followed was so cold that snow lay on the ground for months. Theophanes writes that the starving besiegers ate their horses and camels. Bulgar forces under Khan Tervel, allied with Leo, fell on the Arab camp in Thrace, and Christian crews on the relief fleet deserted. On 15 August 718 Maslama withdrew; storms wrecked much of what was left of the fleet. Constantinople would not face another Muslim siege for almost seven centuries.
story.zh:
717年夏，倭马亚王子马斯拉马率领一支被编年史家称为数十万之众的大军渡过赫勒斯滂海峡，在陆墙外挖掘壕沟，等候庞大的舰队。当年三月刚刚加冕的利奥三世坐镇的这座城市早已为长期围城囤积了粮食。阿拉伯舰队驶过城下进入博斯普鲁斯海峡时，一支拜占庭分舰队用希腊火袭击了它的后卫——这种秘密燃烧剂甚至能在水面上燃烧。

随后的冬天异常寒冷，积雪数月不化。据塞奥法内斯记载，饥饿的围城士兵吃掉了马匹和骆驼。与利奥结盟的保加尔可汗特尔维尔袭击了色雷斯的阿拉伯营地，援军舰队中的基督徒水手纷纷倒戈。718年8月15日马斯拉马撤军，残余舰队又大多毁于风暴。此后近七个世纪，君士坦丁堡再未遭到穆斯林的围攻。

summary.en: Emperors Leo III and Constantine V condemned the veneration of icons, and a council of 754 banned them. The Second Council of Nicaea restored icons in 787, a second iconoclast period followed from 815, and the "Triumph of Orthodoxy" under Empress Theodora in 843 ended the dispute for good.
summary.zh: 利奥三世和君士坦丁五世两位皇帝谴责崇拜圣像，754年的宗教会议明令禁止。787年第二次尼西亚公会议恢复圣像崇拜，815年起又开始第二次破坏圣像时期，直到843年皇后狄奥多拉主持“正统胜利”，争议才最终平息。

sources.title: Leslie Brubaker & John Haldon, Byzantium in the Iconoclast Era c. 680–850: A History (2011)

note: The traditional start date of 726 (removal of the Chalke Gate icon) is questioned by Brubaker and Haldon, who date a firm imperial policy to the 730s.

story.en:
According to later iconophile writers, Leo III began the controversy in 726 by tearing down an image of Christ above the Chalke Gate of the palace, and women of the city killed the officer sent to do it. Modern historians, notably Brubaker and Haldon, think much of this story was written up afterwards by the victors; what is clear is that Leo's son Constantine V argued, in his own theological treatises, that a painted image could not contain Christ's divine nature, and a council at Hieria in 754 condemned icons.

Monks who defended images were persecuted, though the scale of the destruction is debated. In 787 Empress Irene had icon veneration restored at the Second Council of Nicaea; emperors revived iconoclasm in 815. Only in 843, after the death of Emperor Theophilos, did his widow Theodora restore icons for good, an event still celebrated by Orthodox churches on the first Sunday of Lent as the Triumph of Orthodoxy.
story.zh:
据后来拥护圣像的作者记载，利奥三世于726年拆除皇宫铜门上方的基督像，挑起争端，城中妇女杀死了奉命执行的官员。现代史家（尤其是布鲁贝克和霍尔登）认为，这个故事很大程度上是胜利者事后编写的；可以确定的是，利奥之子君士坦丁五世亲自撰写神学论著，主张绘画无法容纳基督的神性，754年希耶里亚会议谴责了圣像。

为圣像辩护的修士遭到迫害，但破坏的规模至今仍有争议。787年皇后伊琳娜通过第二次尼西亚公会议恢复圣像崇拜；815年皇帝们又重启破坏圣像政策。直到843年皇帝狄奥菲洛斯去世，其遗孀狄奥多拉才永久恢复圣像。东正教会至今仍在大斋期第一个主日纪念这一“正统胜利”。

name.en: Battle of Ongal and the founding of Danube Bulgaria
name.zh: 翁加尔之战与多瑙河保加利亚的建立

summary.en: Khan Asparukh's Bulgars defeated the army of Emperor Constantine IV in the Danube delta and crossed into Moesia. In 681 Byzantium agreed to pay tribute, a date traditionally taken as the founding of the First Bulgarian Empire, with its capital at Pliska.
summary.zh: 阿斯帕鲁赫可汗率领的保加尔人在多瑙河三角洲击败君士坦丁四世皇帝的军队，进入默西亚。681年拜占庭同意纳贡，这一年传统上被视为第一保加利亚帝国建立之年，都城设于普利斯卡。

sources.title: Britannica: Bulgaria: The First Bulgarian Empire

note: The battlefield, "Onglos", is placed in the Danube delta area; the exact site is unknown.

summary.en: Emperor Nikephoros I sacked the Bulgar capital Pliska, but Khan Krum trapped his retreating army in a mountain pass and annihilated it. Nikephoros was killed, the first emperor to die in battle since 378, and Krum reportedly had his skull lined with silver as a drinking cup.
summary.zh: 皇帝尼基弗鲁斯一世洗劫了保加尔首都普利斯卡，但克鲁姆可汗在山口围困撤退的拜占庭军并将其全歼。尼基弗鲁斯阵亡，是378年以来首位战死沙场的皇帝；据载克鲁姆把他的头骨镶银做成酒杯。

note: The ambush took place in a pass of the Balkan Mountains (perhaps the Varbitsa pass); coordinates are approximate. The skull cup is reported by Theophanes.

name.en: Cyril and Methodius: the Moravian mission and the Glagolitic alphabet
name.zh: 西里尔与美多德：摩拉维亚传教与格拉哥里字母

summary.en: At Prince Rastislav's request, Emperor Michael III sent the brothers Constantine (Cyril) and Methodius of Thessaloniki to Great Moravia. Constantine created the Glagolitic alphabet, and the brothers translated scripture and liturgy into Slavonic, which Pope Hadrian II approved in 868.
summary.zh: 应拉斯蒂斯拉夫大公之请，皇帝米海尔三世派遣塞萨洛尼基的君士坦丁（西里尔）与美多德兄弟前往大摩拉维亚。君士坦丁创制了格拉哥里字母，兄弟二人把经文和礼仪译成斯拉夫语，868年获教宗哈德良二世批准。

sources.title: Vita Constantini and Vita Methodii (Pannonian Legends)
Francis Dvornik, Byzantine Missions among the Slavs (1970)

note: Located at Mikulčice, one of the main Great Moravian centres; the seat of Rastislav is not securely identified.

story.en:
In 862 Rastislav of Moravia, wary of the Frankish clergy who served his German rivals, asked Constantinople for a teacher who could explain the faith in his people's own language. Emperor Michael III chose two brothers from Thessaloniki, a city where Slavonic was heard in the streets: Constantine, a philosopher and linguist, and Methodius, a former governor turned monk. According to his Life, before setting out Constantine devised a new alphabet, now called Glagolitic, to write Slavonic sounds.

In Moravia the brothers trained disciples and translated the Gospels and the liturgy. Bavarian bishops objected that only Hebrew, Greek and Latin were fit for worship, so in 867–868 the brothers went to Rome, where Pope Hadrian II laid the Slavonic books on the altar of a church. Constantine died in Rome in 869 after taking the monastic name Cyril. Methodius returned as archbishop, endured imprisonment by Frankish clergy, and died in 885; his expelled disciples carried the new letters to Bulgaria.
story.zh:
862年，摩拉维亚大公拉斯蒂斯拉夫不信任为其德意志对手服务的法兰克教士，请求君士坦丁堡派来一位能用本族语言讲解信仰的导师。皇帝米海尔三世选中了来自塞萨洛尼基的一对兄弟——这座城市的街头常能听到斯拉夫语：哲学家兼语言学家君士坦丁，以及由总督转为修士的美多德。据其传记记载，出发前，君士坦丁创制了一套书写斯拉夫语音的新字母，即今天所称的格拉哥里字母。

兄弟二人在摩拉维亚培养门徒，翻译福音书和礼仪经文。巴伐利亚主教们反对说只有希伯来语、希腊语和拉丁语才配用于礼拜，于是兄弟俩在867—868年前往罗马，教宗哈德良二世把斯拉夫文经书供奉在教堂祭坛上。君士坦丁取修道名西里尔，869年在罗马去世。美多德以大主教身份返回，曾遭法兰克教士囚禁，885年去世；被驱逐的门徒们把新文字带到了保加利亚。

summary.en: Khan Boris I accepted baptism from Byzantium, taking the name Michael, and crushed a revolt of boyars loyal to the old religion. After bargaining between Rome and Constantinople he secured an autonomous Bulgarian archbishopric under the Byzantine church in 870.
summary.zh: 鲍里斯一世可汗接受拜占庭的洗礼，取教名米海尔，并镇压了忠于旧信仰的贵族叛乱。他在罗马与君士坦丁堡之间周旋，870年为保加利亚争得隶属拜占庭教会的自主大主教区。

sources.title: Responsa Nicolai I ad consulta Bulgarorum (866)
Florin Curta, Southeastern Europe in the Middle Ages, 500–1250 (2006)

note: The baptism is dated 864 or 865 in the sources.

summary.en: The Primary Chronicle relates that the feuding tribes of the north invited the Varangian Rurik and his brothers to rule them, and that Rurik settled at Novgorod (or Ladoga). Rurik's successors moved south to Kiev, founding the dynasty that ruled Rus' and Muscovy until 1598.
summary.zh: 据《往年纪事》记载，北方相互争斗的部落邀请瓦良格人留里克兄弟前来统治，留里克定居诺夫哥罗德（或拉多加）。其继承者南下基辅，建立了统治罗斯和莫斯科公国直至1598年的王朝。

sources.title: The Russian Primary Chronicle, entry for 6370 (862)
Simon Franklin & Jonathan Shepard, The Emergence of Rus 750–1200 (1996)

note: The chronicle account was compiled around 1113 and its date and details are legendary; archaeology confirms Scandinavian presence at Staraya Ladoga and Rurikovo Gorodishche near Novgorod in the 9th century.

name.en: Preslav school and the Cyrillic alphabet
name.zh: 普雷斯拉夫文学学派与西里尔字母

summary.en: The Council of Preslav in 893 made Slavonic the language of church and state in Bulgaria. In the new capital Preslav, disciples of Methodius developed the Cyrillic alphabet from Greek letters, while Clement of Ohrid taught in the south-west; under Tsar Simeon Bulgaria became the centre of Slavonic letters.
summary.zh: 893年普雷斯拉夫会议确立斯拉夫语为保加利亚教会与国家的语言。在新都普雷斯拉夫，美多德的门徒以希腊字母为基础发展出西里尔字母，克莱门特则在西南部的奥赫里德授徒；西美昂沙皇治下的保加利亚成为斯拉夫文学的中心。

sources.title: Ivan Dujčev, "Preslav school", in The Oxford Dictionary of Byzantium (1991)

note: Who created Cyrillic is debated; it is usually credited to the Preslav circle (perhaps Naum or Constantine of Preslav) around 890–900.

story.en:
When Methodius died in 885, his disciples were driven out of Moravia; some were sold as slaves in Venice. A few, among them Clement and Naum, reached Bulgaria, where Khan Boris I welcomed them. Boris had converted twenty years earlier and needed a native clergy who would not answer to Greek bishops. Clement was sent to Ohrid, where his biography credits him with teaching some 3,500 pupils.

In 893 a council moved the capital from Pliska to Preslav and declared Slavonic the language of the liturgy. Around this time scholars at Preslav adapted Greek capitals, with extra letters for Slavonic sounds, into a simpler script that later generations named Cyrillic after the missionary. Under Boris's son Simeon, Preslav translators turned Byzantine chronicles, sermons and law into Slavonic, and from Bulgaria the script travelled to Serbia and Rus'.
story.zh:
885年美多德去世后，他的门徒被逐出摩拉维亚，一些人甚至在威尼斯被卖为奴隶。其中克莱门特、瑙姆等几人辗转来到保加利亚，受到鲍里斯一世可汗的欢迎。鲍里斯二十年前已皈依基督教，需要一批不受希腊主教节制的本土教士。克莱门特被派往奥赫里德，据其传记记载，他在那里教授了约三千五百名学生。

893年的一次会议将首都由普利斯卡迁至普雷斯拉夫，并宣布斯拉夫语为礼仪语言。大约同时，普雷斯拉夫的学者以希腊大写字母为基础，增添表示斯拉夫语音的字母，形成一套更简便的文字，后人以那位传教士之名称之为西里尔字母。在鲍里斯之子西美昂治下，普雷斯拉夫的译者把拜占庭的编年史、布道文和法律译成斯拉夫语，这种文字也从保加利亚传入塞尔维亚和罗斯。

name.en: Hungarian conquest of the Carpathian Basin
name.zh: 马扎尔人征服喀尔巴阡盆地

summary.en: Pressed by the Pechenegs on the steppe, the seven Magyar tribes under Árpád crossed the Carpathians and occupied the basin between the Danube and Tisza. Their victory over the Bavarians at Pressburg in 907 secured the land that became the Kingdom of Hungary.
summary.zh: 在草原上受到佩切涅格人的压迫，以阿尔帕德为首的马扎尔七部落越过喀尔巴阡山，占据多瑙河与蒂萨河之间的盆地。907年在普雷斯堡击败巴伐利亚人后，他们稳固了这片后来成为匈牙利王国的土地。

label.zh: 翻越韦雷茨克山口
在多瑙河弯一带定居
占领潘诺尼亚

label.en: Victory over the Bavarians at Pressburg
label.zh: 在普雷斯堡击败巴伐利亚人

sources.title: Pál Engel, The Realm of St Stephen: A History of Medieval Hungary 895–1526 (2001)
Constantine VII Porphyrogennetos, De administrando imperio, ch. 38–40

note: The traditional date 895/896 is approximate; the location marks the Verecke Pass where tradition places the crossing.

story.en:
Byzantine and Frankish writers knew the Magyars as fast-moving horsemen on the Pontic steppe who sometimes served as mercenaries. Around 895, while their warriors were away fighting the Bulgarians for the Byzantine emperor, Pecheneg nomads fell on their camps. The survivors, led by the chieftain Árpád, crossed the Carpathians, by later tradition through the Verecke Pass, into a basin weakly held by Great Moravia, Bulgaria and Frankish lords.

Within a few years Great Moravia had collapsed, and in 907 the Magyars destroyed a Bavarian army near Pressburg (Bratislava). For half a century they raided as far as Spain and Italy, until Otto I defeated them on the Lechfeld in 955. Settled and converted, Árpád's descendants made the basin a Christian kingdom in 1000; Hungarians celebrated the thousandth anniversary of the "Conquest of the Homeland" in 1896.
story.zh:
拜占庭和法兰克的作者笔下，马扎尔人是黑海草原上行动迅捷、时常充当雇佣兵的骑手。约895年，他们的战士正为拜占庭皇帝远征保加利亚，佩切涅格游牧民趁机袭击了他们的营地。幸存者在首领阿尔帕德率领下——按后来的传说是经由韦雷茨克山口——翻越喀尔巴阡山，进入一个由大摩拉维亚、保加利亚和法兰克领主薄弱控制的盆地。

几年之内大摩拉维亚崩溃，907年马扎尔人在普雷斯堡（今布拉迪斯拉发）附近歼灭一支巴伐利亚军队。此后半个世纪，他们的劫掠远达西班牙和意大利，直到955年奥托一世在莱希费尔德击败他们。定居并皈依基督教后，阿尔帕德的后裔于1000年在这片盆地建立了基督教王国；1896年匈牙利人隆重纪念了“征服家园”一千周年。

summary.en: Duke Mieszko I of the Polans accepted Latin Christianity, probably on Holy Saturday 966, a year after marrying the Bohemian princess Dobrawa. The conversion brought his realm into Latin Christendom, and a missionary bishopric was founded at Poznań in 968.
summary.zh: 波兰人公爵梅什科一世在迎娶波希米亚公主杜布拉夫卡一年后，大约于966年复活节前夕接受拉丁基督教。这次皈依使其领地融入拉丁基督教世界，968年波兹南设立传教主教区。

sources.title: Norman Davies, God's Playground: A History of Poland, vol. 1 (rev. ed. 2005)

note: The place of baptism is unknown (Poznań, Gniezno or Ostrów Lednicki are proposed); the location is Poznań, seat of the first bishopric.

story.en:
Little is known of Poland before Mieszko I. German chroniclers describe him as a powerful lord east of the Oder, hemmed in by the pagan Veleti, the Saxon march and Bohemia. In 965 he married Dobrawa, daughter of the Czech duke Boleslaus I, and the next year, probably at Easter 966, he was baptised. Thietmar of Merseburg, writing two generations later, gives Dobrawa the credit, saying she wore down her husband's paganism with patience.

The decision was political as well as spiritual. Baptism sealed his alliance with Bohemia against the Veleti and raised his standing in Europe; older histories also saw it as denying German margraves a pretext for missionary war. Mieszko took Latin rather than Byzantine Christianity, tying Poland to Rome. In 968 Jordan became the first missionary bishop at Poznań, and around 991 Mieszko placed his state under papal protection in the document known as Dagome iudex. Poland celebrated its millennium in 1966.
story.zh:
梅什科一世之前的波兰鲜为人知。德意志编年史家称他为奥得河以东的强大领主，周围是信奉异教的维莱蒂人、萨克森边区和波希米亚。965年他迎娶捷克公爵博莱斯拉夫一世之女杜布拉夫卡，次年（大概在966年复活节）受洗。两代人之后写作的梅泽堡的蒂特马尔把功劳归于杜布拉夫卡，说她以耐心消磨了丈夫的异教信仰。

这一决定既关乎信仰，也关乎政治。受洗巩固了他与波希米亚结成的对抗维莱蒂人的同盟，提高了他在欧洲的地位；较早的史家还认为，这使德意志边伯失去了发动“传教战争”的借口。梅什科选择拉丁而非拜占庭基督教，把波兰与罗马联系在一起。968年约尔丹成为波兹南首任传教主教；约991年，梅什科以《达戈梅审判》文书将国家置于教宗保护之下。1966年波兰隆重纪念了建国受洗一千周年。

summary.en: Emperor Otto III made a pilgrimage to the tomb of the martyr Adalbert (Wojciech) at Gniezno, where he honoured Duke Bolesław I as a friend and partner of the Empire and founded the archbishopric of Gniezno, giving Poland its own church province.
summary.zh: 奥托三世皇帝前往格涅兹诺朝拜殉道者阿达尔贝特（沃伊切赫）之墓，在那里尊崇波列斯瓦夫一世公爵为帝国的朋友与伙伴，并设立格涅兹诺大主教区，使波兰拥有独立的教省。

sources.title: Gallus Anonymus, Gesta principum Polonorum I.6

name.en: Kingdom of Hungary founded: coronation of Stephen I
name.zh: 匈牙利王国建立：斯蒂芬一世加冕

summary.en: Grand Prince Stephen, Árpád's descendant, was crowned king at Esztergom with a crown sent by Pope Sylvester II, at Christmas 1000 or New Year 1001. He defeated pagan rivals, founded bishoprics and counties, and turned the Magyar principality into a Christian kingdom.
summary.zh: 阿尔帕德的后裔斯蒂芬大公于1000年圣诞或1001年元旦在埃斯泰尔戈姆以教宗西尔维斯特二世所赐王冠加冕为王。他击败异教对手，设立主教区和州，把马扎尔公国改造为基督教王国。

sources.title: Pál Engel, The Realm of St Stephen (2001)

note: No Wikidata item exists for the coronation itself. The exact date (25 Dec 1000 or 1 Jan 1001) is debated.

story.en:
Stephen was born Vajk, son of the Grand Prince Géza, who had begun to bring in Christian missionaries while remaining, as a chronicler put it, rich enough to sacrifice to both the old gods and the new. Baptised and married to the Bavarian princess Gisela, Stephen inherited the throne in 997 and immediately faced his kinsman Koppány, who claimed it under the old custom of seniority. Stephen defeated him, and had his body quartered and displayed on the gates of four towns.

With the support of Emperor Otto III, Pope Sylvester II sent a crown, and Stephen was anointed king at Esztergom around the turn of the year 1000. He set up an archbishopric there and another at Kalocsa, organised royal counties around castles, and ordered every ten villages to build a church. Canonised in 1083, he became Hungary's patron; 20 August, his feast, is the national day, and the Holy Crown that bears his name is kept in the Parliament in Budapest.
story.zh:
斯蒂芬原名沃伊克，是大公盖佐之子。盖佐已开始引入基督教传教士，但正如一位编年史家所说，他富有得足以同时向旧神和新神献祭。斯蒂芬受洗后娶巴伐利亚公主吉塞拉为妻，997年继承大位，随即面对宗亲科帕尼的挑战——后者依照长者继承的旧俗要求王位。斯蒂芬击败了他，并将其尸体分为四块悬挂在四座城镇的城门上。

在奥托三世皇帝的支持下，教宗西尔维斯特二世送来王冠，约在1000年岁末年初，斯蒂芬在埃斯泰尔戈姆受膏为王。他在那里和卡洛乔设立大主教区，以城堡为中心组建王室州，并命令每十个村庄修建一座教堂。1083年他被封为圣徒，成为匈牙利的主保圣人；他的瞻礼日8月20日是匈牙利国庆日，以他命名的圣冠今天保存在布达佩斯的国会大厦。

summary.en: Emperor Basil II outflanked the fortified Bulgarian line in the Belasitsa mountains and routed Tsar Samuel's army. Byzantine chroniclers say he blinded some 15,000 prisoners, leaving one eye to every hundredth man; Samuel died soon after, and Bulgaria was annexed in 1018.
summary.zh: 巴西尔二世皇帝迂回包抄保加利亚人在贝拉西察山的防线，击溃沙皇萨穆伊尔的军队。拜占庭编年史家称他刺瞎约一万五千名俘虏，每百人留一人一只眼睛引路；萨穆伊尔不久死去，保加利亚于1018年被吞并。

sources.title: John Skylitzes, Synopsis of Histories, Basil II ch. 35
Paul Stephenson, The Legend of Basil the Bulgar-Slayer (2003)

note: The figure of 15,000 blinded prisoners comes from Skylitzes, writing decades later; Stephenson and others consider it exaggerated.

story.en:
For almost thirty years Tsar Samuel, ruling from Ohrid and Prespa, had defied Basil II and even destroyed a Byzantine army at Trajan's Gate in 986. By 1014 Basil was grinding down Bulgarian fortresses year by year. That summer Samuel blocked the Kleidion pass under the Belasitsa range with a wooden palisade. While Basil attacked it from the front, his general Nikephoros Xiphias led troops over the mountain and fell on the Bulgarians from behind.

John Skylitzes, writing about seventy years later, gives the famous aftermath: Basil blinded the captives, leaving one man in every hundred with a single eye to lead the rest home. When they reached Samuel, he collapsed at the sight and died two days later, on 6 October. Modern historians doubt the numbers but not the brutality. Bulgarian resistance ended in 1018, and only much later did Basil acquire the epithet "Bulgar-slayer".
story.zh:
近三十年来，以奥赫里德和普雷斯帕为根据地的沙皇萨穆伊尔一直与巴西尔二世对抗，986年还在图拉真门全歼一支拜占庭军队。到1014年，巴西尔正逐年蚕食保加利亚的要塞。那年夏天，萨穆伊尔用木栅封锁了贝拉西察山下的克雷迪昂山口。巴西尔从正面进攻，他的将领尼基弗鲁斯·希菲亚斯则率兵翻山，从背后袭击保加利亚军。

约七十年后写作的约翰·斯基里齐斯记载了著名的结局：巴西尔刺瞎了俘虏，每百人留一人一只眼睛，领其余人回家。他们回到萨穆伊尔身边时，他见状昏厥，两天后即10月6日死去。现代史家怀疑这个数字，但不怀疑其残酷。保加利亚的抵抗于1018年结束，而“保加利亚人屠夫”这一绰号则是很久以后才加在巴西尔身上的。

summary.en: Yaroslav the Wise built a great cathedral of Holy Wisdom in Kyiv, decorated with Byzantine mosaics and frescoes, as the seat of the metropolitan of Rus'. Its walls carry graffiti from the 11th century onwards, and the cathedral is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
summary.zh: 智者雅罗斯拉夫在基辅修建了一座宏伟的圣智慧大教堂，饰以拜占庭风格的马赛克与壁画，作为罗斯都主教的座堂。其墙壁上留有11世纪以来的涂刻文字，现为联合国教科文组织世界遗产。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage: Kyiv, Saint-Sophia Cathedral and Related Monastic Buildings, Kyiv-Pechersk Lavra
The Russian Primary Chronicle, entry for 6545 (1037)

note: The chronicle dates the foundation to 1037; some historians argue for 1011.

name.en: Founding of the Kyiv Caves Monastery
name.zh: 基辅洞窟修道院的创建

summary.en: The monks Anthony and Theodosius founded a community in caves on the hills above the Dnieper south of Kyiv. The Pechersk Lavra became the leading monastery of Rus', the home of the chronicler Nestor and a burial place of saints whose bodies still lie in its catacombs.
summary.zh: 修士安东尼和费奥多西在基辅以南第聂伯河畔山丘的洞穴中创立修道团体。洞窟修道院后来成为罗斯首屈一指的修道院，是编年史家涅斯托尔的居所，众多圣徒的遗体至今仍安放在其地下墓道中。

note: The traditional founding date of 1051 comes from the Primary Chronicle.

summary.en: An anonymous Old East Slavic poem tells of Prince Igor of Novgorod-Seversky's failed raid against the Polovtsians (Cumans) in 1185 and his escape from captivity. Its lament of Igor's wife Yaroslavna and its call for unity among the princes made it a classic; Borodin based his opera Prince Igor on it.
summary.zh: 这部佚名的古东斯拉夫语诗篇讲述1185年北诺夫哥罗德公伊戈尔征讨波洛韦茨人（库曼人）失败及其从囚禁中脱逃的故事。伊戈尔之妻雅罗斯拉夫娜的哀歌和诗中对诸公团结的呼吁使之成为经典，鲍罗丁据此创作了歌剧《伊戈尔王》。

sources.title: Britannica: The Song of Igor's Campaign
Simon Franklin, "The Igor Tale", in Writing, Society and Culture in Early Rus (2002)

note: The only manuscript burned in Moscow in 1812; a minority of scholars (e.g. Edward Keenan) have argued the poem is an 18th-century forgery, but most accept a late-12th-century date. Located at Novgorod-Seversky.

name.zh: 第四次十字军洗劫君士坦丁堡

summary.en: Diverted by debts to Venice and the promises of the pretender Alexios IV, the Fourth Crusade stormed Constantinople and sacked it for three days. The crusaders crowned Baldwin of Flanders as Latin emperor and divided the empire, while Byzantine successor states arose at Nicaea, Trebizond and in Epirus.
summary.zh: 第四次十字军因欠威尼斯债务、又受觊觎皇位的阿历克塞四世许诺所诱，转而攻陷君士坦丁堡并洗劫三日。十字军拥立佛兰德的鲍德温为拉丁皇帝并瓜分帝国，拜占庭的继承国则在尼西亚、特拉布宗和伊庇鲁斯相继建立。

label.zh: 十字军在威尼斯集结
为威尼斯攻陷扎拉
舰队驶过达达尼尔海峡
第一次围城，阿历克塞四世登基

label.en: Storming and sack of the city
label.zh: 攻城并洗劫

sources.title: Geoffrey of Villehardouin, The Conquest of Constantinople
Niketas Choniates, Historia (O City of Byzantium)
Jonathan Phillips, The Fourth Crusade and the Sack of Constantinople (2004)

story.en:
The Fourth Crusade was meant for Egypt. Its leaders contracted with Venice for ships for 33,500 men, but only about a third turned up, and they could not pay. The aged, nearly blind Doge Enrico Dandolo offered to defer the debt if the army helped Venice retake the Christian port of Zara, and then the exiled prince Alexios Angelos promised money, troops and church union if the crusaders put him on the Byzantine throne.

They did so in 1203, but Alexios IV could not pay and was murdered by a palace rival. On 12–13 April 1204 the crusaders broke in from the Golden Horn. For three days they plundered: the historian Niketas Choniates, who lived through the sack, described soldiers breaking up the altar of Hagia Sophia and a prostitute seated on the patriarch's throne. The bronze horses now in St Mark's, Venice, were among the loot. A Latin Empire was set up, and although Michael VIII retook the city in 1261, Byzantium never recovered its former strength.
story.zh:
第四次十字军原定目标是埃及。首领们与威尼斯签约，租用可运载33,500人的船只，可到场的只有约三分之一，根本付不起船费。年迈且几近失明的总督恩里科·丹多洛提出，只要十字军帮威尼斯夺回基督教港口扎拉，债务可以缓付；随后流亡王子阿历克塞·安格洛斯又许诺，只要十字军扶他登上拜占庭皇位，便给予金钱、军队并实现教会合一。

1203年他们如愿让他登基，但阿历克塞四世无力兑现，被宫廷对手杀害。1204年4月12日至13日，十字军从金角湾破城而入，连续劫掠三天：亲历这场浩劫的史家尼基塔斯·侯尼亚提斯记述，士兵把圣索菲亚大教堂的祭坛砸碎瓜分，一名妓女还坐上了牧首的宝座。如今陈列在威尼斯圣马可大教堂的青铜驷马就是当时的战利品。十字军建立了拉丁帝国；尽管米海尔八世于1261年收复该城，拜占庭再也没有恢复昔日的实力。

summary.en: King Andrew II of Hungary, pressed by his nobles and royal servants, issued a charter guaranteeing their privileges, limiting arbitrary arrest and confiscation and granting a right of resistance if the king broke it. Often compared with Magna Carta, it remained a cornerstone of the Hungarian constitution until 1848.
summary.zh: 匈牙利国王安德烈二世在贵族和王室侍从的压力下颁布特许状，保障其特权，限制任意逮捕与没收财产，并允许在国王违约时进行反抗。它常被拿来与英格兰的《大宪章》相比，直到1848年一直是匈牙利宪制的基石。

sources.title: János M. Bak et al. (eds.), The Laws of the Medieval Kingdom of Hungary, vol. 1 (1989)

note: Issued at the royal diet in Székesfehérvár, used here as the location.

summary.en: Batu and Subutai's armies destroyed Ryazan in December 1237, took Vladimir and killed Grand Prince Yuri II on the Sit River in 1238, then swept the south, storming Chernigov and Pereyaslavl and finally Kyiv in 1240. Most Rus' principalities became tributaries of the Golden Horde for some 240 years.
summary.zh: 拔都和速不台的大军于1237年12月摧毁梁赞，1238年攻陷弗拉基米尔并在西季河畔杀死大公尤里二世，随后横扫南方，攻下切尔尼戈夫和佩列亚斯拉夫尔，1240年最终攻陷基辅。罗斯诸公国大多成为金帐汗国的附庸，长达约240年。

sources.title: Charles J. Halperin, Russia and the Golden Horde (1985)
Peter Jackson, The Mongols and the West (2005)

story.en:
In December 1237, with the rivers frozen into roads, a Mongol army under Batu and the veteran general Subutai appeared before Ryazan. The princes of Rus' had been warned by the defeat on the Kalka fourteen years before, but they did not unite. Ryazan fell after a five-day bombardment; the later Tale of the Destruction of Ryazan says no eye remained open to weep for the dead. Vladimir, capital of the north-east, was stormed in February 1238, the grand prince's family dying in the burning cathedral, and Yuri II himself was killed on the Sit River in March.

By the traditional account the spring thaw saved Novgorod, but the little town of Kozelsk held out for seven weeks; the chronicles say the Mongols called it the "evil city". After a pause on the steppe, the armies turned south: Pereyaslavl and Chernigov fell in 1239 and Kyiv on 6 December 1240. The princes now had to travel to the Horde at Sarai, and sometimes to Karakorum, to receive their patents to rule.
story.zh:
1237年12月，河流冰封成路，拔都和老将速不台率领的蒙古军出现在梁赞城下。十四年前卡尔卡河之败本已向罗斯诸公敲响警钟，他们却仍未联合。梁赞在五天的轰击后陷落，后世的《拔都毁灭梁赞记》说，连一只为死者哭泣的眼睛都没有剩下。1238年2月，东北罗斯的首都弗拉基米尔被攻破，大公家眷死于燃烧的大教堂中；3月，尤里二世本人在西季河畔阵亡。

按传统说法，春季解冻使诺夫哥罗德幸免于难；小城科泽利斯克则坚守了七个星期，据编年史记载，蒙古人称之为“恶城”。在草原休整之后，大军转向南方：1239年佩列亚斯拉夫尔和切尔尼戈夫失陷，1240年12月6日基辅陷落。此后罗斯诸公必须前往萨莱的汗廷，有时甚至远赴哈拉和林，领取统治的册封诏书。

summary.en: A Mongol force raiding Poland defeated the army of Duke Henry II the Pious of Silesia, with Templar, Hospitaller and Moravian contingents, near Legnica. Henry was killed and his head paraded on a spear; the raiders then turned south to join Batu in Hungary.
summary.zh: 一支侵袭波兰的蒙古军在莱格尼察附近击败西里西亚公爵虔诚者亨里克二世及其圣殿骑士、医院骑士和摩拉维亚援军。亨里克阵亡，首级被挑在长矛上示众；蒙古军随后南下，与在匈牙利的拔都会合。

sources.title: Jan Długosz, Annales seu cronicae incliti regni Poloniae, book VII
Peter Jackson, The Mongols and the West (2005)

summary.en: Batu and Subutai's army surprised King Béla IV's Hungarian host at the Sajó river and destroyed it after encircling the royal camp. Béla fled to the Adriatic as the Mongols ravaged Hungary for a year; they withdrew in 1242, probably after news of Ögedei's death and for other strategic reasons.
summary.zh: 拔都和速不台的军队在绍约河畔突袭匈牙利国王贝拉四世的大军，包围王室营地后将其歼灭。贝拉逃往亚得里亚海沿岸，蒙古人在匈牙利肆虐一年，于1242年撤军——可能是得知窝阔台死讯，也有其他战略原因。

sources.title: Master Roger, Carmen miserabile (Epistle of Sorrow)
Thomas of Split, Historia Salonitana, ch. 36–37
Peter Jackson, The Mongols and the West (2005)

story.en:
Béla IV had been warned. He had given refuge to Cuman nomads fleeing the Mongols, but when a mob in Pest killed the Cuman khan Köten, the Cumans rode off plundering, and Béla faced the invasion of 1241 with a divided kingdom. His army camped behind the Sajó river, its wagons chained into a fortress. After a night attack on the bridge was beaten back, at dawn on 11 April the Mongols cleared it with stone-throwing catapults, while Subutai crossed the river further south.

By morning the camp was surrounded. The Mongols left a gap in their ring, and the fleeing Hungarians were cut down along the road to Pest. Thomas of Split wrote that the road was strewn with corpses and the ground dyed red with blood. Béla escaped to Dalmatia, pursued to an island off Trogir. After the Mongols left in 1242 he rebuilt the kingdom with stone castles and new settlers, earning the name of "second founder" of Hungary.
story.zh:
贝拉四世并非没有预警。他收留了逃避蒙古人的库曼游牧民，但佩斯的暴民杀害了库曼可汗科腾，库曼人一路劫掠而去，贝拉只能以一个四分五裂的王国迎战1241年的入侵。他的军队在绍约河后扎营，用铁链连起车辆组成营垒。蒙古人夜袭桥梁被击退后，于4月11日黎明用投石机驱散守桥的匈牙利军，速不台则在更南面渡河。

天亮时营地已被包围。蒙古人在包围圈上故意留出缺口，溃逃的匈牙利人在通往佩斯的路上遭到追杀。斯普利特的托马斯写道，沿路尸横遍野，大地被鲜血染红。贝拉逃往达尔马提亚，一直被追到特罗吉尔外海的小岛上。1242年蒙古人撤走后，他修筑石头城堡、招徕新移民，重建王国，被称为匈牙利的“第二位奠基者”。

summary.en: Prince Alexander Nevsky of Novgorod defeated knights of the Livonian branch of the Teutonic Order and their Estonian levies on frozen Lake Peipus, ending their eastward advance. The battle was small by later standards but became a national legend, above all through Eisenstein's 1938 film.
summary.zh: 诺夫哥罗德公亚历山大·涅夫斯基在冰封的楚德湖上击败条顿骑士团利沃尼亚分团的骑士及其爱沙尼亚兵员，阻止了他们向东扩张。此役规模按后世标准并不大，却成为民族传奇，尤其因爱森斯坦1938年的电影而广为人知。

note: The exact site is unknown; it is usually placed on Lake Lämmijärv (Warm Lake), the narrows between Peipus and Pskov lakes; the Livonian Rhymed Chronicle counts 20 knights killed and 6 captured, far fewer than Russian tradition.

name.zh: 拜占庭收复君士坦丁堡

summary.en: A small Nicaean force under Alexios Strategopoulos slipped into Constantinople through a gate while the Venetian fleet was away, and the Latin emperor Baldwin II fled. Michael VIII Palaiologos entered the city in August, restoring the Byzantine Empire under the Palaiologan dynasty, which ruled until 1453.
summary.zh: 趁威尼斯舰队外出，阿历克塞·斯特拉特戈普洛斯率领的一小支尼西亚部队从一座城门潜入君士坦丁堡，拉丁皇帝鲍德温二世逃走。米海尔八世·巴列奥略于8月入城，在巴列奥略王朝治下恢复了拜占庭帝国，该王朝一直统治到1453年。

sources.title: Deno J. Geanakoplos, Emperor Michael Palaeologus and the West (1959)

name.en: Founding of the University of Prague

summary.en: King Charles IV of Bohemia, soon Holy Roman Emperor, founded a studium generale at Prague with papal approval, the first university in Central Europe. It became a centre of the Hussite reform, was later named Charles University, and remains the Czech Republic's leading university.
summary.zh: 波希米亚国王、不久后成为神圣罗马帝国皇帝的查理四世经教宗批准在布拉格创办大学，这是中欧第一所大学。它后来成为胡斯改革的中心，得名查理大学，至今仍是捷克首屈一指的高等学府。

sources.title: Hilde de Ridder-Symoens (ed.), A History of the University in Europe, vol. 1 (1992)

summary.en: Stefan Dušan, crowned Emperor of the Serbs and Greeks at Skopje in 1346, issued a law code at assemblies in 1349 and 1354. Drawing on Byzantine law and Serbian custom, it regulated the church, nobility, towns and peasants of the short-lived Serbian Empire at its height.
summary.zh: 1346年在斯科普里加冕为“塞尔维亚人与希腊人的皇帝”的斯特凡·杜尚，于1349年和1354年的议会上颁布法典。法典融合拜占庭法与塞尔维亚习惯法，规范了鼎盛时期短命的塞尔维亚帝国的教会、贵族、城市与农民。

sources.title: John V. A. Fine, The Late Medieval Balkans (1987)

summary.en: Grand Prince Dmitry of Moscow led a coalition of Russian princes across the Don and defeated the army of the Horde commander Mamai on Kulikovo Field. Tokhtamysh burned Moscow two years later, but the victory made Moscow the leader of the Russian lands and earned Dmitry the name Donskoy.
summary.zh: 莫斯科大公德米特里率领罗斯诸公联军渡过顿河，在库利科沃原野击败金帐汗国权臣马麦的军队。两年后脱脱迷失火烧莫斯科，但这场胜利使莫斯科成为罗斯诸地的领袖，德米特里也因此得名“顿斯科伊”（顿河的）。

sources.title: Zadonshchina; Chronicle Tale of the Battle with Mamai
Charles J. Halperin, Russia and the Golden Horde (1985)

summary.en: Grand Duke Jogaila of Lithuania agreed to accept Catholic baptism with his people and to marry Poland's young queen Jadwiga in return for the Polish crown. Crowned as Władysław II in 1386, he founded the Jagiellonian dynasty and a Polish–Lithuanian union that lasted four centuries.
summary.zh: 立陶宛大公约盖拉同意本人及其臣民接受天主教洗礼，并迎娶年轻的波兰女王雅德维加，以换取波兰王冠。1386年他加冕为瓦迪斯瓦夫二世，开创雅盖隆王朝及延续四百年的波兰—立陶宛联合。

summary.en: Prince Lazar's Serbian army and Bosnian allies met the Ottomans under Sultan Murad I on the Field of Blackbirds. Both rulers were killed, Murad reportedly by the knight Miloš Obilić. The outcome was indecisive, but Serbia soon became an Ottoman vassal, and the battle became the core of Serbian epic memory.
summary.zh: 拉扎尔大公的塞尔维亚军及其波斯尼亚盟军在“黑鸟之野”迎战苏丹穆拉德一世统率的奥斯曼军。双方君主均战死，据说穆拉德为骑士米洛什·奥比利奇所杀。战斗胜负未分，但塞尔维亚不久沦为奥斯曼附庸，这场战役成为塞尔维亚史诗记忆的核心。

sources.title: Thomas A. Emmert, Serbian Golgotha: Kosovo, 1389 (1990)
Noel Malcolm, Kosovo: A Short History (1998)

note: Date given in the Julian calendar (15 June 1389); Serbs commemorate it on Vidovdan, 28 June (Gregorian).

story.en:
On St Vitus's Day, 15 June 1389 (Julian calendar; the feast is now kept on 28 June), Prince Lazar Hrebeljanović, the strongest of the Serbian lords left after the collapse of Dušan's empire, faced Sultan Murad I on the plain of Kosovo near Priština. Lazar had Bosnian troops sent by King Tvrtko under Vlatko Vuković, and his son-in-law Vuk Branković commanded a wing. Little reliable detail of the fighting survives. Both Murad and Lazar died: the sultan was stabbed in or near his tent, according to most accounts by a Serbian noble later named Miloš Obilić, and Lazar was captured and beheaded. Murad's son Bayezid took command.

The early news reached Florence and Paris as a Christian victory, and militarily it may have been a draw. But Serbia had lost its prince and many nobles, and Lazar's widow Milica soon accepted Ottoman vassalage. Over the following centuries church cults and folk epics turned Lazar into a martyr who chose the heavenly kingdom over the earthly one, and Vidovdan became a central date of Serbian national identity.
story.zh:
1389年儒略历6月15日圣维特节（该节日如今在6月28日纪念），杜尚帝国崩溃后最强大的塞尔维亚领主拉扎尔·赫雷别利亚诺维奇大公，在普里什蒂纳附近的科索沃平原迎战苏丹穆拉德一世。拉扎尔麾下有波斯尼亚国王特夫尔特科派来、由弗拉特科·武科维奇统率的援军，他的女婿武克·布兰科维奇指挥一翼。关于战斗过程，可靠的细节所存无几。穆拉德与拉扎尔双双殒命：多数记载称苏丹在营帐中或附近被一名塞尔维亚贵族刺杀，此人后来被称为米洛什·奥比利奇；拉扎尔被俘后遭斩首。穆拉德之子巴耶济德接掌了指挥权。

最初传到佛罗伦萨和巴黎的消息是基督徒获胜，从军事上看或许是平局。但塞尔维亚失去了君主和许多贵族，拉扎尔的遗孀米利察不久便接受奥斯曼宗主权。此后数百年间，教会崇拜和民间史诗把拉扎尔塑造成舍弃尘世王国而选择天国的殉道者，维多夫丹（圣维特节）也成为塞尔维亚民族认同的核心日子。

summary.en: A crusading army of Hungarians under King Sigismund, French and Burgundian knights and others, besieging the Danube fortress of Nicopolis, was crushed by Sultan Bayezid I and his Serbian vassal Stefan Lazarević. The defeat ended large-scale western crusades against the Ottomans for half a century.
summary.zh: 由匈牙利国王西吉斯蒙德率领、包括法兰西和勃艮第骑士在内的十字军围攻多瑙河要塞尼科波利斯，被苏丹巴耶济德一世及其塞尔维亚附庸斯特凡·拉扎雷维奇击溃。此后半个世纪，西欧再未对奥斯曼发动大规模十字军。

sources.title: Aziz S. Atiya, The Crusade of Nicopolis (1934)

summary.en: After Jan Hus was burned at Constance and Prague radicals threw councillors from the New Town Hall windows in 1419, Bohemian Hussites defeated five crusades. Jan Žižka's wagon forts and handguns beat imperial knighthood, until moderate Utraquists crushed the radical Taborites at Lipany in 1434 and came to terms with the Church.
summary.zh: 扬·胡斯在康斯坦茨被处火刑，1419年布拉格激进派又把议员从新城市政厅的窗户扔下，此后波希米亚胡斯派连续击退五次十字军。扬·杰式卡的车阵和手铳击败了帝国骑士，直到1434年温和的饼酒同领派在利帕尼击溃激进的塔博尔派，与教会达成和解。

label.zh: 布拉格新城市政厅抛窗事件
维特科夫山之战
塔博尔城建立
德意志布罗德（哈夫利奇库夫布罗德）大捷
奥西希（拉贝河畔乌斯季）之战

塔博尔派在利帕尼战败

sources.title: Thomas A. Fudge, The Crusade against Heretics in Bohemia, 1418–1437 (2002)

story.en:
Jan Hus, a Prague preacher who attacked the sale of indulgences and the wealth of the clergy, went to the Council of Constance in 1414 under a safe-conduct from King Sigismund and was burned as a heretic on 6 July 1415. In Bohemia his followers took communion "in both kinds", bread and wine, with the chalice as their emblem. On 30 July 1419 a procession led by the priest Jan Želivský stormed Prague's New Town Hall and threw the Catholic councillors from the windows to their deaths.

When Sigismund, heir to the Bohemian crown, launched a crusade in 1420, the one-eyed squire Jan Žižka turned peasants and townsmen into a formidable army. His wagons, chained together and bristling with handguns and small cannon, broke charges of armoured knights; crusaders reportedly fled at Domažlice in 1431 at the sound of the Hussite hymn. Žižka, totally blind by then, died in 1424, traditionally of plague, though modern historians doubt it. The movement split, and at Lipany in 1434 the moderates destroyed the radicals, opening the way to a compromise that left Bohemia with its own church for two centuries.
story.zh:
布拉格传道人扬·胡斯抨击兜售赎罪券和教士敛财，1414年持西吉斯蒙德国王颁发的安全通行证赴康斯坦茨公会议，却于1415年7月6日被当作异端烧死。在波希米亚，他的追随者坚持领受饼和酒“两种圣餐”，以圣杯为标志。1419年7月30日，神父扬·哲利夫斯基率领的游行队伍冲进布拉格新城市政厅，把天主教议员从窗口扔下摔死。

1420年，波希米亚王位继承人西吉斯蒙德发动十字军，独眼骑士扬·杰式卡把农民和市民训练成一支劲旅。他用铁链连接的战车布满手铳和小炮，击溃了身披重甲的骑士冲锋；据说1431年在多马日利采，十字军一听到胡斯派的圣歌就溃逃了。杰式卡1424年去世，那时他已双目失明；传统说法称他死于瘟疫，但现代史家对此存疑。运动随后分裂，1434年在利帕尼，温和派歼灭了激进派，由此达成妥协，使波希米亚保有自己的教会长达两个世纪。

summary.en: The last major crusade of the era, led by the young King Władysław III of Poland and Hungary and John Hunyadi, was destroyed by Sultan Murad II near the Black Sea port of Varna. Władysław died charging the sultan's janissaries, and the Ottoman hold on the Balkans was confirmed nine years before the fall of Constantinople.
summary.zh: 这一时期最后一次大规模十字军由年轻的波兰兼匈牙利国王瓦迪斯瓦夫三世和匈雅提·亚诺什率领，在黑海港口瓦尔纳附近被苏丹穆拉德二世击溃。瓦迪斯瓦夫在冲击苏丹禁卫军时阵亡，奥斯曼对巴尔干的控制由此巩固，九年后君士坦丁堡陷落。

sources.title: Colin Imber, The Crusade of Varna, 1443–45 (2006)

summary.en: Three years after taking Constantinople, Mehmed II besieged the Hungarian border fortress of Belgrade. John Hunyadi broke the Ottoman river blockade and, with the crusading peasants of the friar John of Capistrano, routed the besiegers. Hunyadi died of plague weeks later; the noon bells ordered by the pope are often linked to the victory.
summary.zh: 攻占君士坦丁堡三年后，穆罕默德二世围攻匈牙利边境要塞贝尔格莱德。匈雅提·亚诺什突破奥斯曼人的河上封锁，与修士卡皮斯特拉诺的约翰召集的十字军农民一道击溃围城之敌。数周后匈雅提死于瘟疫；教宗下令敲响的正午钟声常被与这次胜利联系在一起。

sources.title: Franz Babinger, Mehmed the Conqueror and His Time (1978)
Pál Engel, The Realm of St Stephen (2001)

note: Pope Callixtus III ordered the noon bell before the battle, as a call to prayer; it later came to commemorate the victory.

name.en: Great Stand on the Ugra River

summary.en: Khan Akhmat of the Great Horde marched on Moscow to enforce tribute, but Ivan III's army held the crossings of the Ugra. After weeks facing each other across the river, both sides withdrew as winter came. The standoff is traditionally taken as the end of the "Tatar yoke" over Russia.
summary.zh: 大帐汗国的阿合马汗进军莫斯科，企图强征贡赋，伊凡三世的军队扼守乌格拉河渡口。双方隔河对峙数周后，随着冬季来临各自撤退。这次对峙传统上被视为罗斯摆脱“鞑靼枷锁”的标志。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Great Stand on the Ugra River

note: The Great Horde was the successor of the Golden Horde, linked here.

summary.en: Sultan Suleiman the Magnificent's army destroyed the Hungarian royal army on the Danube plain at Mohács in under two hours. King Louis II drowned in a stream as he fled; Hungary was split between the Habsburgs and a Transylvanian-based rival king, and Buda fell to the Ottomans in 1541.
summary.zh: 苏丹苏莱曼一世的军队在莫哈奇的多瑙河平原上不到两小时便歼灭了匈牙利王军。国王路易二世逃跑时溺死在溪流中；匈牙利随后被哈布斯堡家族与以特兰西瓦尼亚为根据地的对立国王瓜分，布达于1541年落入奥斯曼人之手。

sources.title: Géza Perjés, The Fall of the Medieval Kingdom of Hungary: Mohács 1526 – Buda 1541 (1989)
Pál Fodor, The Battle of Mohács 1526 (Research Centre for the Humanities, Budapest, 2019)

story.en:
By 1526 the Kingdom of Hungary, the great power of Matthias Corvinus's day, was bankrupt and torn between magnate factions. When Suleiman marched up the Danube with perhaps 50,000 to 60,000 men and heavy artillery, the twenty-year-old Louis II could gather only around 25,000. With Archbishop Pál Tomori, a friar turned general, in command, the war council chose to give battle on the open plain south of Mohács rather than wait for reinforcements from Transylvania and Croatia.

On the afternoon of 29 August the Hungarian heavy cavalry charged and broke into the Ottoman line, only to be torn apart by the guns and janissaries waiting in prepared positions behind it. Within about two hours most of the army, seven bishops and much of the nobility lay dead. Louis fell from his horse crossing the swollen Csele stream and drowned in his armour. Hungary then had two kings, Ferdinand of Habsburg and John Zápolya, and for 150 years it was divided between Habsburg, Ottoman and Transylvanian rule. Hungarians still say "more was lost at Mohács" of a minor misfortune.
story.zh:
到1526年，马加什·科尔温时代称雄一方的匈牙利王国已国库空虚、豪门党争不断。苏莱曼率五六万大军和重炮沿多瑙河北上时，二十岁的路易二世只集结了约两万五千人。由修士转任将领的大主教托莫里·帕尔统领全军，作战会议决定在莫哈奇以南的开阔平原上决战，而不等待特兰西瓦尼亚和克罗地亚的援军。

8月29日下午，匈牙利重骑兵发起冲锋，突入奥斯曼阵线，却被阵后预设阵地中的火炮和禁卫军撕得粉碎。大约两个小时内，大部分军队、七位主教和许多贵族战死。路易渡过涨水的切莱溪时坠马，身披盔甲溺水而亡。此后匈牙利同时出现两位国王——哈布斯堡家族的斐迪南和扎波利亚·亚诺什，在一百五十年间被哈布斯堡、奥斯曼和特兰西瓦尼亚三方分割统治。匈牙利人至今遇到小挫折时还会说：“在莫哈奇失去的更多。”

summary.en: Tsar Ivan IV besieged Kazan, capital of the Tatar khanate on the middle Volga, with some 150,000 men, and his engineers blew breaches in the walls with mines. The fall of Kazan, followed by Astrakhan in 1556, opened the Volga route and the way to Siberia, and was celebrated by building St Basil's Cathedral in Moscow.
summary.zh: 沙皇伊凡四世率约十五万大军围攻伏尔加河中游鞑靼汗国的首都喀山，工兵用地雷炸开城墙缺口。喀山陷落、1556年阿斯特拉罕亦被征服，打通了伏尔加河航道和通往西伯利亚之路；莫斯科为纪念此役修建了圣瓦西里大教堂。

sources.title: Matthew P. Romaniello, The Elusive Empire: Kazan and the Creation of Russia, 1552–1671 (2012)

note: The troop figure is a traditional estimate.

summary.en: Ivan IV withdrew to Alexandrova Sloboda and returned only after being granted a personal domain, the oprichnina, policed by black-clad oprichniki. They purged boyars, murdered Metropolitan Philip and in 1570 killed thousands of Novgorod's inhabitants, before Ivan abolished the system in 1572.
summary.zh: 伊凡四世退居亚历山德罗夫村，直到获准设立个人领地“特辖区”才返回莫斯科，由身着黑衣的特辖军维持秩序。他们清洗大贵族，杀害都主教菲利普，1570年在诺夫哥罗德杀害数千居民，1572年伊凡才废除这一制度。

sources.title: Isabel de Madariaga, Ivan the Terrible (2005)
Heinrich von Staden, The Land and Government of Muscovy (memoir of an oprichnik)

summary.en: Count Nikola Zrinski (Miklós Zrínyi) held the small Hungarian fortress of Szigetvár for over a month against Suleiman the Magnificent's last campaign, then led a final sortie in which he was killed. The sultan died in his tent during the siege, and the defence became a heroic legend for Croats and Hungarians.
summary.zh: 兹里尼·米克洛什（克罗地亚语称尼古拉·兹林斯基）伯爵率众坚守匈牙利小要塞锡盖特堡一个多月，抵御苏莱曼一世的最后一次远征，最终率部突围战死。苏丹在围城期间死于营帐中，这次守城成为克罗地亚人和匈牙利人的英雄传奇。

sources.title: Pál Fodor & Géza Dávid (eds.), Ottomans, Hungarians and Habsburgs in Central Europe (2000)

summary.en: The printer Ivan Fedorov, who had produced Moscow's first dated book, the Apostol of 1564, printed the first complete Bible in Church Slavonic at Ostroh in Volhynia under the patronage of Prince Konstantyn Ostrozky. It became the standard Orthodox Slavonic text.
summary.zh: 曾在1564年印出莫斯科第一部有确切日期的书籍《使徒行传》的印刷商伊凡·费奥多罗夫，在沃伦地区的奥斯特罗赫得到康斯坦丁·奥斯特罗日斯基公爵资助，印出第一部完整的教会斯拉夫语圣经。它成为东正教斯拉夫语圣经的标准文本。

summary.en: Most Orthodox bishops of the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, meeting at Brest, accepted the authority of the pope while keeping their Byzantine rite, creating the Ruthenian Uniate (today's Ukrainian and Belarusian Greek Catholic) Church. Opponents held a rival synod, and the split fed religious conflict for generations.
summary.zh: 波兰—立陶宛联邦的大多数东正教主教在布列斯特集会，承认教宗权威但保留拜占庭礼仪，由此形成罗塞尼亚合一教会（即今乌克兰和白俄罗斯希腊礼天主教会）。反对者召开对立会议，这一分裂引发了延续数代的宗教冲突。

sources.title: Borys A. Gudziak, Crisis and Reform: The Kyivan Metropolitanate, the Patriarchate of Constantinople, and the Genesis of the Union of Brest (1998)

summary.en: The end of the Rurikid line, a catastrophic famine in 1601–1603 and rival pretenders claiming to be Ivan IV's dead son Dmitry plunged Muscovy into civil war, with Polish and Swedish intervention. A militia raised by Kuzma Minin and Prince Dmitry Pozharsky expelled the Poles from Moscow in 1612, and Michael Romanov was elected tsar in 1613.
summary.zh: 留里克王朝绝嗣、1601—1603年的大饥荒以及多个冒充伊凡四世早夭之子德米特里的僭位者，使莫斯科国陷入内战，波兰和瑞典亦出兵干涉。1612年库济马·米宁和德米特里·波扎尔斯基公爵组织的民军把波兰人逐出莫斯科，1613年米哈伊尔·罗曼诺夫被推选为沙皇。

label.zh: 伪德米特里一世进入莫斯科

label.en: Second False Dmitry's camp at Tushino
label.zh: 伪德米特里二世的图希诺营地
波兰人在克卢希诺获胜

label.en: Minin and Pozharsky raise a militia in Nizhny Novgorod
label.zh: 米宁与波扎尔斯基在下诺夫哥罗德组建民军
波兰人被逐出克里姆林宫
米哈伊尔·罗曼诺夫当选沙皇（在科斯特罗马接受）

sources.title: Chester S. L. Dunning, Russia's First Civil War: The Time of Troubles and the Founding of the Romanov Dynasty (2001)
Maureen Perrie, Pretenders and Popular Monarchism in Early Modern Russia (1995)

story.en:
When Tsar Fyodor I, Ivan the Terrible's feeble son, died childless in 1598, the Rurikid line, which traced its rule back more than seven centuries, ended. The regent Boris Godunov was elected tsar, but volcanic weather brought frosts in summer 1601, and in the famine that followed perhaps a third of Muscovy's people died. Rumours spread that Ivan's youngest son Dmitry, who had died at Uglich in 1591, had survived. In 1605 a pretender claiming to be him entered Moscow with Polish backing; he was murdered within a year, but more "Dmitrys" followed.

Boyar factions, Cossack hosts and peasant rebels fought across the land. After defeating the Russians at Klushino in 1610, a Polish garrison occupied the Kremlin, and Sweden seized Novgorod. In Nizhny Novgorod the butcher Kuzma Minin collected money for a national militia and invited Prince Dmitry Pozharsky to lead it; in late 1612 they starved the Poles out of the Kremlin. An assembly of the land elected sixteen-year-old Michael Romanov tsar in 1613, beginning a dynasty that ruled for three centuries. The liberation is now marked by Russia's Unity Day on 4 November.
story.zh:
1598年，伊凡雷帝体弱的儿子费奥多尔一世无嗣而终，可追溯七百多年的留里克世系就此断绝。摄政鲍里斯·戈杜诺夫被推选为沙皇，但火山喷发造成的异常天气使1601年夏天出现霜冻，随之而来的饥荒中，莫斯科国或许有三分之一的人口死亡。谣言四起，说1591年死于乌格利奇的伊凡幼子德米特里其实还活着。1605年，一个自称德米特里的僭位者在波兰支持下进入莫斯科；不到一年他便被杀，但更多的“德米特里”接踵而来。

大贵族派系、哥萨克军团和农民起义者在各地混战。1610年波兰人在克卢希诺击败俄军后，一支波兰驻军占领了克里姆林宫，瑞典则夺取了诺夫哥罗德。在下诺夫哥罗德，肉商库济马·米宁为民军募集资金，并请德米特里·波扎尔斯基公爵出任统帅；1612年底，他们困死了克里姆林宫里的波兰人。1613年，缙绅会议推选十六岁的米哈伊尔·罗曼诺夫为沙皇，开启了延续三百年的王朝。如今俄罗斯以11月4日“人民团结日”纪念这次解放。

summary.en: Outside Prague, the army of the Catholic League and Emperor Ferdinand II routed the Bohemian Protestant estates and their elected king Frederick V of the Palatinate in about an hour. Twenty-seven rebel leaders were executed on the Old Town Square in 1621, and Bohemia was re-Catholicised under Habsburg rule.
summary.zh: 在布拉格城外，天主教联盟和斐迪南二世皇帝的军队仅用约一小时便击溃了波希米亚新教等级会议及其推选的国王普法尔茨的腓特烈五世。1621年二十七名叛乱领袖在老城广场被处决，波希米亚在哈布斯堡统治下被重新天主教化。

sources.title: Peter H. Wilson, Europe's Tragedy: A History of the Thirty Years War (2009)

summary.en: Hetman Bohdan Khmelnytsky led the Zaporozhian Cossacks, allied with the Crimean Tatars, in a revolt against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth that created a Cossack state in central Ukraine. Tens of thousands of Jews and Poles were massacred. In 1654 at Pereiaslav the Cossacks accepted the protection of the Russian tsar.
summary.zh: 盖特曼博赫丹·赫梅利尼茨基率领扎波罗热哥萨克，联合克里米亚鞑靼人反抗波兰—立陶宛联邦，在乌克兰中部建立哥萨克国家。数以万计的犹太人和波兰人遭到屠杀。1654年在佩列亚斯拉夫，哥萨克接受了俄国沙皇的保护。

若夫季沃季大捷
科尔孙大捷

sources.title: Serhii Plokhy, The Cossacks and Religion in Early Modern Ukraine (2001)
Paul Robert Magocsi, A History of Ukraine (2nd ed. 2010)
Shaul Stampfer, "What Actually Happened to the Jews of Ukraine in 1648?", Jewish History 17 (2003)

note: Estimates of Jewish deaths range from about 18,000–20,000 (Stampfer) to far higher figures in contemporary chronicles.

story.en:
Bohdan Khmelnytsky was a middle-aged Cossack officer, educated by the Jesuits, when a Polish neighbour seized his estate at Subotiv, his son was beaten, and the courts gave him no redress. Late in 1647 he fled to the Zaporozhian Sich on the lower Dnieper, won the Crimean khan as an ally, and in May destroyed two Polish armies at Zhovti Vody and Korsun. Peasants across Ukraine rose against Polish landlords, Catholic clergy and the Jewish leaseholders who managed estates for them.

The violence was immense. Hebrew chroniclers such as Nathan Hannover recorded massacres in towns like Nemyriv and Tulchyn; modern estimates of Jewish deaths vary widely, recent studies putting them at about 18,000–20,000. Khmelnytsky entered Kyiv in triumph at the start of 1649 and ruled a Cossack Hetmanate, but when his Tatar allies deserted him at Berestechko in 1651, he sought another protector. At Pereiaslav in January 1654 the Cossack officers swore allegiance to Tsar Alexis, an agreement that Russian and Ukrainian historians have interpreted very differently ever since.
story.zh:
博赫丹·赫梅利尼茨基是一位受过耶稣会教育的中年哥萨克军官。一位波兰邻居强占了他在苏博季夫的庄园，他的儿子遭到毒打，法庭却不给他公道。1647年底，他逃往第聂伯河下游的扎波罗热营地，争取到克里米亚汗为盟友，5月在若夫季沃季和科尔孙接连歼灭两支波兰军队。乌克兰各地农民纷纷起来反抗波兰地主、天主教教士以及替地主经营庄园的犹太承租人。

暴力规模骇人。内森·汉诺威等希伯来编年史家记录了涅米里夫、图利钦等城镇的屠杀；现代学者对犹太人死亡人数的估计差别很大，近年研究多认为约在1.8万至2万人之间。1649年初，赫梅利尼茨基凯旋进入基辅，统治着一个哥萨克盖特曼国；然而1651年在别列斯捷奇科，鞑靼盟友临阵脱逃，他只得另寻保护者。1654年1月在佩列亚斯拉夫，哥萨克军官们宣誓效忠沙皇阿列克谢，此后俄罗斯和乌克兰史家对这一协定的解读大相径庭。

summary.en: After the Ottoman defeat at Vienna in 1683 and sixteen years of war with the Holy League, the Ottomans signed peace at Karlowitz (Sremski Karlovci). They ceded most of Hungary and Transylvania to the Habsburgs, Podolia to Poland and the Morea to Venice, their first major permanent loss of territory in Europe.
summary.zh: 1683年奥斯曼军在维也纳战败，又与神圣同盟苦战十六年后，奥斯曼在卡尔洛维茨（今斯雷姆斯基卡尔洛夫奇）签订和约。他们把匈牙利大部和特兰西瓦尼亚割给哈布斯堡家族，把波多利亚交还波兰，把摩里亚割给威尼斯，这是奥斯曼在欧洲首次大规模永久丧失领土。

sources.title: Caroline Finkel, Osman's Dream: The History of the Ottoman Empire (2005)

summary.en: During the Great Northern War Peter the Great laid the Peter and Paul Fortress on Hare Island in the Neva delta, newly taken from Sweden. Built by conscripted labourers at great human cost, the city became Russia's capital in 1712 and its "window on Europe".
summary.zh: 大北方战争期间，彼得大帝在刚从瑞典手中夺得的涅瓦河三角洲兔子岛上奠基彼得保罗要塞。这座城市由被强征的劳工付出巨大生命代价建成，1712年成为俄国首都和“通向欧洲的窗口”。

sources.title: Lindsey Hughes, Russia in the Age of Peter the Great (1998)
UNESCO World Heritage: Historic Centre of Saint Petersburg

note: Uses the QID of the Peter and Paul Fortress, whose foundation on 16/27 May 1703 marks the founding of the city.

story.en:
In May 1703 Russian troops took the small Swedish fort of Nyenskans near the mouth of the Neva. Peter I wanted a harbour on the Baltic, and on 16 May (27 May in the new style) the foundations of a wooden fortress were laid on Hare Island. A legend that Peter cut two strips of turf with a bayonet and an eagle circled overhead was written down later and is probably embellished.

The site was a marsh flooded by autumn storms. Each year tens of thousands of peasants, soldiers and Swedish prisoners were sent to drain it, drive piles and dig canals, and many died of disease and cold; the number is unknown, and later claims of 30,000 to 100,000 dead are probably exaggerated. Peter forbade stone building elsewhere in Russia so that masons would come, and ordered nobles to build houses in the new town. In 1712 the court moved from Moscow. Pushkin's Bronze Horseman later turned the city's mixture of imperial grandeur and human cost into poetry.
story.zh:
1703年5月，俄军攻下涅瓦河口附近的瑞典小要塞尼恩斯堪斯。彼得一世想要一个波罗的海港口，于是在5月16日（新历27日）在兔子岛上为一座木制要塞奠基。所谓彼得用刺刀割下两块草皮、一只鹰在头顶盘旋的传说是后来才写下的，恐怕经过了渲染。

这里原是秋季风暴常常淹没的沼泽。每年有成千上万的农民、士兵和瑞典战俘被派来排水、打桩、开挖运河，许多人死于疾病和严寒；确切人数无从得知，后世所说的三万至十万死者恐怕言过其实。彼得禁止俄国其他地方兴建石头建筑，好让石匠都来这里，又命令贵族在新城建房。1712年宫廷从莫斯科迁来。后来普希金在《青铜骑士》中把这座城市帝国的宏伟与人的代价写成了诗篇。

summary.en: In three partitions (1772, 1793, 1795) Russia, Prussia and Austria divided the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth between them, despite the reforming Constitution of 3 May 1791 and Kościuszko's uprising of 1794. Poland vanished from the map until 1918.
summary.zh: 俄国、普鲁士和奥地利通过三次瓜分（1772年、1793年、1795年）把波兰—立陶宛联邦分割殆尽，尽管波兰在1791年通过了改革性的《五三宪法》，并在1794年爆发柯斯丘什科起义。此后波兰从地图上消失，直到1918年。

sources.title: Jerzy Lukowski, The Partitions of Poland: 1772, 1793, 1795 (1999)

story.en:
By the 18th century the Commonwealth was large but weak: its elected kings had little power, and any single deputy could break up the Sejm with the liberum veto. Russia treated it as a protectorate, placing Catherine the Great's former lover Stanisław August Poniatowski on the throne in 1764. In 1772, to settle a crisis over Russian gains against the Ottomans, Prussia, Russia and Austria each took a slice of Polish territory, about a third of the whole.

The shock produced a remarkable reform movement. On 3 May 1791 the Four-Year Sejm adopted a constitution abolishing the veto and strengthening the monarchy, the first codified national constitution in Europe. Catherine answered with invasion and a second partition in 1793. Tadeusz Kościuszko led a national uprising in 1794, winning at Racławice with scythe-armed peasants, but he was wounded and captured at Maciejowice, and Russian troops stormed Warsaw's suburb of Praga. In 1795 the remnant was divided, and in 1797 the three powers agreed that even the name of Poland should be abolished.
story.zh:
到18世纪，联邦幅员辽阔却十分虚弱：选举产生的国王权力很小，任何一名议员都能以“自由否决权”解散议会。俄国把它当作保护国，1764年把叶卡捷琳娜大帝的旧情人斯坦尼斯瓦夫·奥古斯特·波尼亚托夫斯基扶上王位。1772年，为化解俄国对奥斯曼战争所获利益引发的危机，普鲁士、俄国和奥地利各自割走一块波兰领土，合计约占全境的三分之一。

震惊之下，波兰兴起了一场引人注目的改革运动。1791年5月3日，“四年议会”通过宪法，废除否决权、加强王权，这是欧洲第一部成文的国家宪法。叶卡捷琳娜以入侵作答，1793年第二次瓜分波兰。1794年，塔德乌什·柯斯丘什科领导全民起义，率手持镰刀的农民在拉茨瓦维采获胜，但在马切约维采负伤被俘，俄军随后血洗华沙郊区布拉加。1795年残余领土被瓜分，1797年三国更约定连“波兰”这一国名也要废除。

summary.en: The Don Cossack Yemelyan Pugachev, claiming to be the murdered Tsar Peter III, raised Yaik Cossacks, Bashkirs, Ural factory serfs and Volga peasants in the largest peasant war in Russian history. His forces burned Kazan in 1774 before government troops defeated him; he was betrayed and executed in Moscow in 1775.
summary.zh: 顿河哥萨克叶梅利扬·普加乔夫冒称已遇害的沙皇彼得三世，发动亚伊克哥萨克、巴什基尔人、乌拉尔工厂农奴和伏尔加农民，掀起俄国历史上规模最大的农民战争。1774年起义军焚烧喀山，后被政府军击败；普加乔夫遭出卖，1775年在莫斯科被处决。

Alexander Pushkin, The History of Pugachev (1834)

summary.en: Tadeusz Kościuszko proclaimed a national insurrection in Kraków's Market Square against Russia and Prussia. Peasant scythemen helped win at Racławice and he promised to ease serfdom, but he was captured at Maciejowice, Suvorov stormed Praga, and the defeat led to the third partition.
summary.zh: 塔德乌什·柯斯丘什科在克拉科夫中央广场宣布发动反抗俄国和普鲁士的全民起义。手持镰刀的农民协助取得拉茨瓦维采大捷，他也承诺减轻农奴制，但他在马切约维采被俘，苏沃洛夫攻陷布拉加，失败导致了第三次瓜分。

sources.title: Alex Storozynski, The Peasant Prince: Thaddeus Kosciuszko and the Age of Revolution (2009)

summary.en: On the day troops swore allegiance to the new Tsar Nicholas I, about 3,000 soldiers led by liberal officers refused and formed up on Senate Square in St Petersburg, demanding a constitution. Nicholas dispersed them with artillery; five leaders were hanged and over a hundred exiled to Siberia, some followed by their wives.
summary.zh: 在军队向新沙皇尼古拉一世宣誓效忠的那一天，约三千名士兵在自由派军官带领下拒绝宣誓，在圣彼得堡枢密院广场列队，要求立宪。尼古拉用大炮驱散了他们；五名领导者被绞死，一百多人被流放西伯利亚，其中一些人的妻子随夫同往。

sources.title: Anatole G. Mazour, The First Russian Revolution, 1825 (1937)

note: Date given in the Gregorian calendar (14 December 1825 Old Style).

summary.en: Young officer cadets in Warsaw attacked the residence of Grand Duke Constantine, and the Congress Kingdom of Poland rose against Russian rule, deposing Nicholas I as king. After battles at Grochów and Ostrołęka the Russians retook Warsaw in September 1831; thousands of Poles, many of the nation's political and cultural elite among them, went into the "Great Emigration", chiefly to France.
summary.zh: 华沙的青年军校学员袭击康斯坦丁大公官邸，波兰会议王国起而反抗俄国统治，宣布废黜尼古拉一世的波兰王位。经过格罗胡夫和奥斯特罗文卡等战役，俄军于1831年9月重占华沙；数千名波兰人（其中有许多政治和文化精英）流亡国外，主要去往法国，史称“大移民”。

sources.title: Piotr S. Wandycz, The Lands of Partitioned Poland, 1795–1918 (1974)

summary.en: Britain, France, the Ottoman Empire and Sardinia fought Russia, chiefly by besieging the naval base of Sevastopol for almost a year. Disease killed more soldiers than battle; Florence Nightingale's nursing and some of the earliest war photographs and telegraphed reports changed public views of war. The Peace of Paris (1856) neutralised the Black Sea.
summary.zh: 英国、法国、奥斯曼帝国和撒丁王国联合对俄作战，主要是围攻塞瓦斯托波尔海军基地近一年。死于疾病的士兵多于战死者；南丁格尔的护理工作以及最早一批战地照片和电报新闻改变了公众对战争的看法。1856年的《巴黎和约》使黑海中立化。

label.zh: 巴拉克拉瓦与轻骑兵的冲锋
因克尔曼之战
塞瓦斯托波尔陷落（马拉霍夫岗）

sources.title: Orlando Figes, Crimea: The Last Crusade (2010)

note: polity-kingdom-of-france is used for France for lack of a Second Empire record.

story.en:
The quarrel began over who should hold the keys of churches in Bethlehem and Jerusalem, and over Tsar Nicholas I's claim to protect the Ottoman sultan's Orthodox subjects. When Russia occupied the Danubian principalities and sank an Ottoman squadron at Sinop in 1853, Britain and France, alarmed at Russian power at the Straits, declared war in March 1854. In September 1854 their armies landed in the Crimea to destroy the Black Sea Fleet's base at Sevastopol.

The siege lasted 349 days. A cavalry misunderstanding at Balaklava sent the British Light Brigade charging into Russian guns, immortalised by Tennyson. In the hospitals at Scutari Florence Nightingale's nurses fought cholera and filth, while William Howard Russell's dispatches in The Times exposed the army's mismanagement. On the Russian side a young artillery officer, Leo Tolstoy, wrote the Sevastopol Sketches. The French stormed the Malakhov redoubt in September 1855 and the city fell. Defeat convinced the new tsar, Alexander II, that Russia needed reform, beginning with serfdom.
story.zh:
争端起于伯利恒和耶路撒冷教堂钥匙的归属，以及沙皇尼古拉一世自称有权保护奥斯曼苏丹治下的东正教臣民。1853年俄国占领多瑙河公国，并在锡诺普击沉一支奥斯曼舰队，担忧俄国控制海峡的英国和法国于1854年3月宣战。1854年9月，英法军队登陆克里米亚，目标是摧毁黑海舰队的基地塞瓦斯托波尔。

围城持续了349天。巴拉克拉瓦的一次骑兵命令误会，让英国轻骑兵旅冲向俄军炮口，丁尼生的诗使之不朽。在斯库塔里的医院里，南丁格尔的护士们与霍乱和污秽搏斗，《泰晤士报》记者威廉·霍华德·拉塞尔的通讯揭露了军队的管理混乱。在俄方，一位年轻的炮兵军官列夫·托尔斯泰写下了《塞瓦斯托波尔故事》。1855年9月法军攻占马拉霍夫岗，城市陷落。战败使新沙皇亚历山大二世相信俄国必须改革，首先就是农奴制。

name.en: Emancipation of the serfs in Russia

summary.en: Tsar Alexander II's manifesto freed some 23 million privately owned serfs, who gained personal liberty and land allotments but had to pay for them through decades of redemption payments to the state, usually through the village commune. The reform opened an era of "Great Reforms" in courts, local government and the army.
summary.zh: 沙皇亚历山大二世颁布宣言，解放约2300万私有农奴。他们获得人身自由和份地，但须通过村社在数十年内向国家缴纳赎金。这场改革开启了司法、地方自治和军队等领域的“大改革”时代。

sources.title: Daniel Field, The End of Serfdom: Nobility and Bureaucracy in Russia, 1855–1861 (1976)
David Moon, The Abolition of Serfdom in Russia, 1762–1907 (2001)

note: Signed on 19 February 1861 (Old Style), i.e. 3 March in the Gregorian calendar.

story.en:
"It is better to abolish serfdom from above than to wait until it begins to abolish itself from below," Alexander II told Moscow nobles in 1856, after the humiliation of the Crimean War. Committees of landowners and officials argued for five years over how much land the peasants should receive and who would pay. On 19 February 1861 (Old Style), the sixth anniversary of his accession, the tsar signed the manifesto; it was read out in churches across the empire in March.

Peasants were no longer the property of their masters and could marry, trade and go to court. But they often received less land than they had farmed before, and the state compensated the nobles, charging the peasants redemption payments spread over 49 years. Many villagers, expecting a "true freedom" with all the land, refused to believe the decree; at Bezdna in Kazan province troops fired on a crowd and killed dozens. The redemption dues were cancelled only in 1907.
story.zh:
克里米亚战争的屈辱之后，亚历山大二世于1856年对莫斯科贵族说：“与其坐等农奴制自下而上地自行废除，不如自上而下地废除它。”地主与官员组成的委员会为农民应得多少土地、由谁出钱争论了五年。1861年2月19日（旧历）——他登基六周年之日——沙皇签署宣言，3月在全国各地教堂宣读。

农民不再是主人的财产，可以自主婚嫁、经商和诉讼。但他们分得的土地往往少于此前耕种的面积，国家向贵族支付补偿，再让农民在49年内分期缴纳赎金。许多村民原以为会得到包括全部土地的“真正的自由”，拒不相信这份诏书；在喀山省的别兹德纳村，军队向人群开枪，打死数十人。赎金直到1907年才被取消。

summary.en: Triggered by forced conscription of young Poles into the Russian army, an underground National Government led a guerrilla insurrection in Russian Poland and Lithuania. It lasted over a year but was crushed; Romuald Traugutt and other leaders were hanged at the Warsaw Citadel, and Russification followed.
summary.zh: 由于俄国强征波兰青年入伍，一个地下“国民政府”在俄属波兰和立陶宛领导游击起义。起义坚持了一年多但终遭镇压；罗穆亚尔德·特劳古特等领导人在华沙城堡被绞死，随后推行俄罗斯化政策。

sources.title: Piotr S. Wandycz, The Lands of Partitioned Poland, 1795–1918 (1974)

summary.en: Writing a chemistry textbook in St Petersburg, Dmitri Mendeleev arranged the 63 known elements by atomic weight and saw their properties repeat periodically. He left gaps and predicted the properties of undiscovered elements; the discovery of gallium (1875), scandium (1879) and germanium (1886) vindicated his system.
summary.zh: 德米特里·门捷列夫在圣彼得堡编写化学教科书时，把当时已知的63种元素按原子量排列，发现其性质呈周期性重复。他在表中留下空位，预言了未知元素的性质；镓（1875年）、钪（1879年）和锗（1886年）的发现证实了他的体系。

sources.title: Michael D. Gordin, A Well-Ordered Thing: Dmitrii Mendeleev and the Shadow of the Periodic Table (2004)
Royal Society of Chemistry: Development of the periodic table

note: Uses the QID of the periodic table itself. Dated by the Old Style calendar to 17 February 1869 (1 March New Style).

story.en:
In early 1869 Mendeleev, a professor at St Petersburg University, was racing to finish the second volume of his textbook Principles of Chemistry and needed a logical order in which to describe the elements. On 17 February (Old Style), according to the usual account, he put off a trip to inspect cheese dairies and spent the day on the table; the image of him laying out element cards like patience is unconfirmed. A popular story says the final pattern came to him in a dream; Gordin and other historians note that the surviving drafts show a day of hard working-out.

His table placed elements with similar properties in the same column, and where the sequence broke down he trusted the pattern over the data, correcting atomic weights and leaving blanks for "eka-aluminium", "eka-boron" and "eka-silicon". When the French chemist Lecoq de Boisbaudran found gallium in 1875, Mendeleev pointed out that its density must be higher than reported; a remeasurement proved him right. Element 101, mendelevium, was later named in his honour.
story.zh:
1869年初，圣彼得堡大学教授门捷列夫正赶写教科书《化学原理》第二卷，需要一种合乎逻辑的顺序来介绍各种元素。按通常的说法，2月17日（旧历）他推迟了视察奶酪厂的行程，用一整天推敲这张表；至于他像玩纸牌接龙那样摆放元素卡片的情景，则无从证实。流行的故事说最后的规律是他在梦中得到的；戈尔丁等史家指出，留存的草稿表明那是一整天的艰苦推演。

他的周期表把性质相似的元素排在同一列；当顺序与数据不符时，他宁可相信规律，修正原子量，并为“类铝”“类硼”“类硅”留下空位。1875年法国化学家勒科克·德布瓦博德兰发现镓，门捷列夫指出它的密度应高于报告值，重新测量证明他是对的。第101号元素钔后来便以他的名字命名。

name.en: Siege of Plevna and the liberation of Bulgaria
name.zh: 普列文之围与保加利亚解放

summary.en: In the Russo-Turkish War of 1877–1878 Osman Pasha's Ottoman garrison held Plevna (Pleven) for five months against Russian and Romanian armies. Its surrender opened the Balkan passes; the Treaty of San Stefano created a large autonomous Bulgaria, cut back at the Congress of Berlin later in 1878.
summary.zh: 1877—1878年俄土战争中，奥斯曼帕夏率领的奥斯曼守军在普列文坚守五个月，抵抗俄国和罗马尼亚军队。普列文投降后巴尔干山口洞开；《圣斯特凡诺条约》建立了一个幅员辽阔的自治保加利亚，同年晚些时候的柏林会议又将其削减。

sources.title: R. J. Crampton, A Concise History of Bulgaria (2nd ed. 2005)

summary.en: On "Bloody Sunday", 22 January 1905, troops fired on a peaceful procession led by the priest Georgy Gapon to petition the tsar. Strikes, peasant risings, the Potemkin mutiny and a general strike forced Nicholas II's October Manifesto promising civil liberties and an elected Duma, though the regime later curtailed it.
summary.zh: 1905年1月22日“流血星期日”，军队向神父格奥尔吉·加蓬带领前往向沙皇请愿的和平队伍开枪。罢工、农民起义、“波将金”号兵变和总罢工迫使尼古拉二世颁布《十月宣言》，承诺公民自由和选举产生的杜马，但政权后来又加以限制。

label.zh: 冬宫前的流血星期日

label.en: Ivanovo textile strike and first soviet
label.zh: 伊万诺沃纺织工人罢工与第一个苏维埃
敖德萨“波将金”号战舰兵变

label.en: October general strike; St Petersburg Soviet
label.zh: 十月总罢工，圣彼得堡苏维埃
莫斯科普列斯尼亚十二月起义

sources.title: Abraham Ascher, The Revolution of 1905: A Short History (2004)

note: Bloody Sunday was 9 January 1905 Old Style.

story.en:
Defeat in the war with Japan and years of hunger and repression had made Russia restless. Early on Sunday 9 January 1905 (Old Style), tens of thousands of St Petersburg workers with their families, carrying icons and portraits of the tsar, marched behind the priest Georgy Gapon to present a petition at the Winter Palace asking for an eight-hour day and a constituent assembly. Nicholas II was not in the city. Troops opened fire at several points; official figures gave about 96 to 130 dead, other estimates far more.

The myth of the "little father" tsar never recovered. Through 1905 strikes spread, peasants burned manor houses, the sailors of the battleship Potemkin mutinied and steamed into Odessa, and in October a general strike shut the railways. Workers formed councils, soviets, the most famous in St Petersburg, where Leon Trotsky was a leading figure. Nicholas conceded the October Manifesto with an elected Duma, then crushed the Moscow uprising in December. The revolution failed, but it was, as Lenin later said, a dress rehearsal for 1917.
story.zh:
对日战争的失败，加上多年的饥饿与镇压，使俄国人心浮动。1905年1月9日（旧历）星期日清晨，数万名圣彼得堡工人携家带口，手持圣像和沙皇画像，跟随神父格奥尔吉·加蓬前往冬宫递交请愿书，要求八小时工作制和召开立宪会议。尼古拉二世当时并不在城中。军队在多处开枪；官方公布的死亡人数约为96至130人，其他估计则高得多。

“沙皇老爹”的神话从此破灭。整个1905年，罢工蔓延，农民焚烧庄园，“波将金”号战舰水兵哗变后驶入敖德萨，10月的总罢工使铁路陷于瘫痪。工人组建了被称为“苏维埃”的委员会，其中最著名的是圣彼得堡苏维埃，托洛茨基是其主要领导人之一。尼古拉被迫颁布《十月宣言》，设立民选杜马，随后在12月镇压了莫斯科起义。这场革命失败了，但正如列宁后来所说，它是1917年的一次“总演习”。

summary.en: In the First Balkan War Serbia, Bulgaria, Greece and Montenegro drove the Ottomans out of almost all their European lands; Albania declared independence. Quarrelling over Macedonia, Bulgaria then attacked its allies and lost the Second Balkan War. Serbia's gains alarmed Austria-Hungary and helped set the stage for 1914.
summary.zh: 第一次巴尔干战争中，塞尔维亚、保加利亚、希腊和黑山几乎把奥斯曼人赶出了其全部欧洲领土，阿尔巴尼亚宣布独立。随后保加利亚因马其顿问题进攻盟友，在第二次巴尔干战争中落败。塞尔维亚的扩张令奥匈帝国不安，为1914年的大战埋下伏笔。

summary.en: Gavrilo Princip, a Bosnian Serb student in the Young Bosnia movement armed with help from Serbian military intelligence officers, shot the heir to the Habsburg throne and his wife Sophie in Sarajevo. Austria-Hungary's ultimatum to Serbia set off the chain of mobilisations that became the First World War.
summary.zh: “青年波斯尼亚”运动成员、波斯尼亚塞族学生加夫里洛·普林西普在塞尔维亚军方情报官员协助下获得武器，在萨拉热窝枪杀了哈布斯堡皇位继承人及其妻子索菲。奥匈帝国随后向塞尔维亚发出最后通牒，引发一连串动员，最终演变为第一次世界大战。

sources.title: Britannica: Assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand
Christopher Clark, The Sleepwalkers: How Europe Went to War in 1914 (2012)

story.en:
Franz Ferdinand came to Sarajevo to watch army manoeuvres, and his state visit fell on 28 June, St Vitus's Day, the anniversary of Kosovo, which Serb nationalists took as a provocation. Six young conspirators waited along the Appel Quay, armed with bombs and pistols supplied through the Serbian secret society known as the Black Hand. One threw a bomb that bounced off the archduke's car and wounded officers in the car behind.

After a tense reception at the town hall, the archduke decided to visit the wounded in hospital. His driver, not told of the change of route, turned into Franz Joseph Street by the Latin Bridge and stopped to reverse, a few feet from where Gavrilo Princip, nineteen, happened to be standing. Princip fired twice, hitting Sophie in the abdomen and Franz Ferdinand in the neck; both died within minutes. Vienna, backed by Berlin, sent Serbia an ultimatum designed to be refused, and within six weeks the great powers of Europe were at war.
story.zh:
斐迪南大公来萨拉热窝观看军事演习，他的国事访问恰逢6月28日——圣维特节、科索沃战役纪念日，塞尔维亚民族主义者视之为挑衅。六名年轻的密谋者沿阿佩尔河岸大街埋伏，炸弹和手枪来自塞尔维亚秘密组织“黑手会”。其中一人投出的炸弹从大公座车上弹开，炸伤了后车的军官。

在市政厅经过一场紧张的接待后，大公决定去医院探望伤员。司机没有接到改变路线的通知，在拉丁桥旁拐进弗朗茨·约瑟夫街，又停车倒车，恰好停在十九岁的加夫里洛·普林西普站立处几步之外。普林西普开了两枪，分别击中索菲的腹部和斐迪南的颈部，两人在几分钟内相继死去。维也纳在柏林支持下向塞尔维亚发出一份注定被拒绝的最后通牒，六周之内，欧洲列强便陷入了战争。

summary.en: Bread queues and strikes in Petrograd turned into mass demonstrations; when the garrison mutinied and joined the crowds, Nicholas II abdicated on 15 March 1917, ending three centuries of Romanov rule. A Provisional Government shared power uneasily with the Petrograd Soviet until the Bolshevik seizure of power in November.
summary.zh: 彼得格勒的排队抢购面包和罢工演变为大规模示威；驻军哗变并加入人群后，尼古拉二世于1917年3月15日退位，结束了罗曼诺夫王朝三百年的统治。临时政府与彼得格勒苏维埃艰难地分享权力，直到11月布尔什维克夺取政权。

sources.title: Tsuyoshi Hasegawa, The February Revolution, Petrograd, 1917 (2nd ed. 2017)

note: Events of 23 February–2 March 1917 Old Style (8–15 March New Style).

story.en:
By the winter of 1916–1917 Russia had lost millions of men in the war, and Petrograd was short of bread and fuel. On 23 February (Old Style), International Women's Day, women textile workers walked out and called on the metalworkers to join them. Within two days some 200,000 people were on the streets. Nicholas II, at army headquarters in Mogilev, ordered the disorders stopped by force, and on 26 February soldiers fired on crowds.

That night the men of the Volynsky Regiment decided they would not shoot again. Next morning they mutinied, other units followed, and the arsenal and prisons were thrown open. Duma politicians formed a Provisional Committee while workers and soldiers elected the Petrograd Soviet in the same Tauride Palace. Generals told the tsar that the army would not support him, and on 2 March, in his train near Pskov, Nicholas abdicated for himself and his son. His brother Michael declined the throne the next day.
story.zh:
到1916—1917年冬，俄国已在战争中损失数百万兵员，彼得格勒缺粮缺燃料。2月23日（旧历）国际妇女节，纺织女工罢工离厂，号召金属工人加入。两天之内，上街人数达到约20万。身在莫吉廖夫大本营的尼古拉二世下令以武力平息骚乱，2月26日士兵向人群开枪。

当天夜里，沃伦团的士兵决定不再开枪。次日清晨他们哗变，其他部队纷纷响应，军火库和监狱被打开。杜马政治家组成临时委员会，工人和士兵则在同一座塔夫利达宫里选出彼得格勒苏维埃。将军们告诉沙皇军队不会支持他，3月2日，在普斯科夫附近的专列上，尼古拉替自己和儿子宣布退位。次日，他的弟弟米哈伊尔也拒绝了皇位。

summary.en: After the October Revolution the Bolsheviks' Red Army, organised by Trotsky, fought White armies, nationalist movements, peasant insurgents and foreign interventions across the former empire. Red Terror and White pogroms, famine and epidemics killed millions; the Bolshevik victory led to the founding of the Soviet Union in 1922.
summary.zh: 十月革命后，托洛茨基组建的布尔什维克红军在前帝国全境与白军、民族主义运动、农民起义军以及外国干涉军作战。红色恐怖、白军集体迫害、饥荒和瘟疫夺去数百万人的生命；布尔什维克的胜利促成了1922年苏联的成立。

保卫察里津
