红军进入符拉迪沃斯托克

sources.title: Evan Mawdsley, The Russian Civil War (2nd ed. 2007)

story.en:
The Bolsheviks seized Petrograd in October 1917 but held little beyond the cities of central Russia. After they dissolved the elected Constituent Assembly in January 1918 and signed away Ukraine, the Baltic and much of Belarus at Brest-Litovsk, opposition gathered on every side: former tsarist officers on the Don, the Czechoslovak Legion along the Trans-Siberian railway, Admiral Kolchak in Omsk, General Denikin in the south, and British, French, American and Japanese troops at the ports.

Trotsky, as war commissar, rode an armoured train from front to front, conscripting former imperial officers under the eye of political commissars. The Whites never agreed on a programme or on the nations' right to independence, and peasants feared they would bring back the landlords. In July 1918 the Bolsheviks shot Nicholas II and his family in Yekaterinburg. By 1920 Denikin and Kolchak had been beaten; Wrangel's last army sailed from the Crimea in November. Estimates of the dead run from about seven to twelve million, mostly civilians, many of hunger and disease.
story.zh:
布尔什维克于1917年10月夺取彼得格勒，但控制的地区不过是俄罗斯中部的城市。1918年1月他们解散民选的立宪会议，又在布列斯特—立托夫斯克割让乌克兰、波罗的海地区和白俄罗斯大部，反对力量随即四起：顿河的前沙皇军官、沿西伯利亚大铁路分布的捷克斯洛伐克军团、鄂木斯克的高尔察克海军上将、南方的邓尼金将军，以及驻扎在各港口的英、法、美、日军队。

托洛茨基身为陆海军人民委员，乘装甲列车往返各条战线，在政治委员的监督下征召前帝国军官。白军始终没有统一的纲领，也不承认各民族的独立权利，农民则担心他们会把地主带回来。1918年7月，布尔什维克在叶卡捷琳堡枪决了尼古拉二世一家。到1920年邓尼金和高尔察克均已失败，弗兰格尔的最后一支军队于11月从克里米亚撤走。据估计，内战死亡人数约七百万至一千二百万，大多是平民，许多人死于饥饿和疾病。

summary.en: As Tukhachevsky's Red Army approached Warsaw in the Polish–Soviet War, Józef Piłsudski struck its exposed flank from the Wieprz river and routed it. Poles call it the "Miracle on the Vistula"; the Peace of Riga in 1921 fixed Poland's eastern border until 1939.
summary.zh: 波苏战争中，图哈切夫斯基的红军逼近华沙，约瑟夫·毕苏斯基从维普日河出击其暴露的侧翼并将其击溃。波兰人称之为“维斯瓦河奇迹”；1921年的《里加和约》确定了波兰东部边界，一直维持到1939年。

sources.title: Norman Davies, White Eagle, Red Star: The Polish–Soviet War 1919–20 (1972)

note: polity-soviet-union is used for Soviet Russia, which formally predates the USSR (1922).

summary.en: Forced collectivisation, impossible grain quotas, blacklisting of villages and a ban on peasants leaving Soviet Ukraine and the Kuban caused a famine in which around 3.5–5 million people died in Ukraine. Ukraine and many other states recognise it as a genocide; Soviet authorities denied it for decades.
summary.zh: 强制集体化、无法完成的粮食征购指标、把村庄列入“黑名单”以及禁止农民离开苏维埃乌克兰和库班等措施，造成一场大饥荒，乌克兰约有350万至500万人死亡。乌克兰和许多国家承认其为种族灭绝；苏联当局数十年间一直否认。

sources.title: Anne Applebaum, Red Famine: Stalin's War on Ukraine (2017)
Andrea Graziosi, "The Soviet 1931–1933 Famines and the Ukrainian Holodomor", Harvard Ukrainian Studies 27 (2004–2005)

note: Death toll estimates for Ukraine range from about 3.5 to 5 million; whether it legally constitutes genocide is debated among historians, though recognised as such by Ukraine and many parliaments. Located at Poltava, in one of the worst-hit regions.

story.en:
Stalin's first Five-Year Plan required grain to feed the cities and to export for machinery. From 1929 peasants were driven into collective farms, and the better-off, labelled kulaks, were deported. Harvests fell, but in 1932 Moscow kept Ukraine's procurement quota high. Villages that fell short were placed on "blacklists" and stripped of all food, and the "law of five ears" of August 1932 punished the theft of even a handful of grain from collective fields.

In January 1933 a directive signed by Stalin and Molotov ordered the police to stop peasants leaving Ukraine and the Kuban in search of bread. By spring people were dying in their homes and along the roads; children were abandoned at railway stations. Historians' estimates for Ukraine range from about 3.5 to 5 million deaths, and millions more died in Kazakhstan and Russia. Soviet officials denied the famine, as did some Western journalists, while others, such as Gareth Jones, reported it. Ukraine commemorates the victims on the fourth Saturday of November.
story.zh:
斯大林的第一个五年计划需要粮食养活城市，并出口换取机器。1929年起农民被赶进集体农庄，较富裕者被扣上“富农”帽子遭到流放。收成下降，但1932年莫斯科仍给乌克兰定下很高的征购指标。未完成任务的村庄被列入“黑名单”，所有食物被搜走；1932年8月的“五穗法”规定，哪怕从集体农田里偷一把谷穗也要受惩处。

1933年1月，斯大林和莫洛托夫签署的一份指令命令警察阻止乌克兰和库班的农民外出寻找面包。到春天，人们死在家中和路旁，孩子被遗弃在火车站。史家估计乌克兰的死亡人数约为350万至500万，哈萨克斯坦和俄罗斯也有数百万人饿死。苏联官员否认饥荒的存在，一些西方记者也附和否认，另一些人如加雷斯·琼斯则如实报道。乌克兰在每年11月的第四个星期六悼念遇难者。

summary.en: Stalin's terror swept through the Communist Party, the army command and the population at large. Show trials in Moscow condemned old Bolsheviks such as Zinoviev, Kamenev and Bukharin; under NKVD chief Yezhov some 1.5 million people were arrested in 1937–1938 and about 680,000 of them shot.
summary.zh: 斯大林的恐怖席卷共产党、军队指挥层乃至广大民众。莫斯科的公审判处季诺维也夫、加米涅夫、布哈林等老布尔什维克死刑；在内务人民委员叶若夫主持下，1937—1938年约150万人被捕，其中约68万人被枪决。

sources.title: Oleg V. Khlevniuk, The History of the Gulag (2004)
Robert Conquest, The Great Terror: A Reassessment (1990)

note: NKVD records opened in the 1990s give about 1.55 million arrests and some 680,000 executions in 1937–1938.

story.en:
The murder of the Leningrad party chief Sergei Kirov in December 1934 gave Stalin the pretext for a widening hunt for "enemies of the people". In August 1936 Zinoviev and Kamenev, once Lenin's closest colleagues, confessed in court to absurd conspiracies and were shot. Further show trials followed in 1937 and 1938, ending with Nikolai Bukharin. In June 1937 Marshal Tukhachevsky and other top commanders were tried in secret and executed, and much of the officer corps was arrested.

The terror reached far beyond the elite. NKVD Order No. 00447 of July 1937 set quotas, region by region, for shooting and imprisoning former kulaks and "anti-Soviet elements"; separate "national operations" targeted Poles, Germans and others. Prisoners were beaten into naming accomplices, so arrests multiplied. Late in 1938 Stalin ended the mass operations and blamed the excesses on Yezhov, who was himself shot in 1940.
story.zh:
1934年12月，列宁格勒党组织领导人基洛夫遇刺，给了斯大林不断扩大搜捕“人民公敌”的借口。1936年8月，曾是列宁最亲密同事的季诺维也夫和加米涅夫在法庭上承认荒诞的阴谋罪名，随即被枪决。1937年和1938年又接连举行公审，最后一场的被告是尼古拉·布哈林。1937年6月，图哈切夫斯基元帅等高级将领经秘密审判被处决，大批军官被捕。

恐怖远远超出了上层精英。1937年7月的内务人民委员部第00447号命令为各地区规定了枪决和关押前富农及“反苏分子”的指标；另有针对波兰人、德意志人等民族的“民族行动”。囚犯在酷刑下被迫供出“同谋”，逮捕人数因此成倍增长。1938年底，斯大林叫停大规模行动，把过火之处归咎于叶若夫，后者本人也于1940年被枪决。

summary.en: On Stalin's and the Politburo's orders of March 1940, the NKVD shot some 22,000 Polish officers, police, officials and intellectuals taken prisoner after the Soviet invasion of 1939, in the Katyn forest near Smolensk, at Kalinin (Tver), Kharkiv and elsewhere. The USSR blamed Germany until admitting responsibility in 1990.
summary.zh: 根据斯大林和苏共政治局1940年3月的命令，内务人民委员部在斯摩棱斯克附近的卡廷森林、加里宁（特维尔）、哈尔科夫等地枪杀了约2.2万名在1939年苏联入侵后被俘的波兰军官、警察、官员和知识分子。苏联一直嫁祸德国，直到1990年才承认责任。

sources.title: Anna M. Cienciala, Natalia S. Lebedeva & Wojciech Materski (eds.), Katyn: A Crime Without Punishment (2007)

story.en:
When the Red Army invaded eastern Poland on 17 September 1939, it took some 250,000 Polish soldiers prisoner. Many rank-and-file soldiers were released or handed over to the Germans, but about 15,000 officers, police and border guards were held in three special camps at Kozelsk, Starobilsk and Ostashkov. Many officers were reservists in civilian life: doctors, lawyers, teachers and engineers.

On 5 March 1940 the NKVD chief Lavrentiy Beria proposed that they and thousands of prisoners in western Ukraine and Belarus be shot as "hardened enemies of Soviet power", and Stalin and other Politburo members signed his memorandum. In April and May the Kozelsk prisoners were taken to the Katyn forest near Smolensk, those from Ostashkov to Kalinin and those from Starobilsk to Kharkiv, and killed with a shot to the back of the head: 21,857 people in all.

When German forces announced the discovery of the Katyn graves in April 1943, Moscow blamed the Germans and broke off relations with the Polish government in exile, which had asked for a Red Cross inquiry. The lie stood for almost fifty years. In April 1990 the Soviet Union admitted NKVD responsibility, and in 1992 Russia handed Poland copies of the 1940 orders.
story.zh:
1939年9月17日红军入侵波兰东部，俘虏约25万名波兰军人。许多普通士兵获释或被移交德方，但约1.5万名军官、警察和边防人员被关押在科泽利斯克、斯塔罗别尔斯克和奥斯塔什科夫三处特别战俘营。许多军官是预备役人员，平日里是医生、律师、教师和工程师。

1940年3月5日，内务人民委员部首脑拉夫连季·贝利亚提议，把这些人连同乌克兰西部和白俄罗斯西部监狱中的数千名囚犯作为“苏维埃政权的死敌”枪决，斯大林和其他政治局委员在他的报告上签了字。4月至5月间，科泽利斯克的战俘被押往斯摩棱斯克附近的卡廷森林，奥斯塔什科夫的战俘被押往加里宁，斯塔罗别尔斯克的战俘被押往哈尔科夫，从脑后一枪处决，总计21857人。

1943年4月德国宣布发现卡廷墓葬，莫斯科嫁祸德国人，并以流亡伦敦的波兰政府要求红十字会调查为由与之断交。这一谎言维持了近五十年。1990年4月苏联承认内务人民委员部负有责任，1992年俄罗斯向波兰移交了1940年命令的副本。

name.en: Auschwitz and the Holocaust in occupied Poland
name.zh: 奥斯维辛与被占领波兰的大屠杀

summary.en: At Auschwitz-Birkenau near Oświęcim, the largest Nazi German camp complex, about 1.1 million people were murdered, around a million of them Jews, along with Poles, Roma and Soviet prisoners. Together with Treblinka, Sobibór, Bełżec and other killing centres in occupied Poland, it was the heart of the Holocaust. Soviet troops liberated it on 27 January 1945.
summary.zh: 在奥斯维辛附近的奥斯维辛—比克瑙——纳粹德国最大的集中营群——约110万人被杀害，其中约100万是犹太人，此外还有波兰人、罗姆人和苏联战俘。它与被占领波兰境内的特雷布林卡、索比堡、贝乌热茨等灭绝营一起构成大屠杀的核心。1945年1月27日苏军解放了这里。

sources.title: United States Holocaust Memorial Museum: Auschwitz
Franciszek Piper, Auschwitz: How Many Perished (1992)

story.en:
Auschwitz was set up in 1940 in former Polish army barracks at Oświęcim, a town annexed to the Reich, as a concentration camp for Polish political prisoners. In 1941 a far larger camp was begun at nearby Brzezinka, Birkenau, and the SS first tested Zyklon B on Soviet prisoners of war. From 1942 trains brought Jews from across occupied Europe. On the ramp at Birkenau SS doctors selected a minority for forced labour; the rest, including almost all children and the elderly, were sent directly to gas chambers disguised as showers.

In the spring and summer of 1944, during the deportation of Hungary's Jews, some 400,000 people arrived in under two months. Prisoners of the Sonderkommando rose in revolt in October 1944 and blew up a crematorium. As the Red Army approached in January 1945 the SS marched some 56,000–58,000 prisoners west in the snow; when Soviet soldiers entered on 27 January they found some 7,000 left behind. That date is now International Holocaust Remembrance Day.
story.zh:
奥斯维辛集中营于1940年在被并入德国的奥斯维辛镇一处前波兰军营内建立，最初关押波兰政治犯。1941年，附近的布热津卡（比克瑙）开始兴建规模大得多的营地，党卫队首次在苏联战俘身上试验齐克隆B毒气。1942年起，列车从被占领欧洲各地运来犹太人。在比克瑙的站台上，党卫队医生挑出少数人从事强迫劳动，其余的人——包括几乎所有儿童和老人——被直接送进伪装成淋浴间的毒气室。

1944年春夏驱逐匈牙利犹太人期间，不到两个月就有约40万人被运抵这里。1944年10月，“特遣队”囚犯发动起义，炸毁了一座焚尸场。1945年1月红军逼近时，党卫队押着约5.6万至5.8万名囚犯在雪地中向西行进；1月27日苏军士兵进入营地时，发现留下的约有7000人。这一天如今是国际大屠杀纪念日。

summary.en: German and Finnish forces cut Leningrad off by land from September 1941 to January 1944, some 872 days. Starvation, cold and bombardment killed an estimated 650,000 to over a million civilians; supplies came only across Lake Ladoga, by boat in summer and over the frozen "Road of Life" in winter.
summary.zh: 1941年9月至1944年1月，德国和芬兰军队从陆上封锁列宁格勒约872天。饥饿、严寒和炮击估计造成65万至逾百万平民死亡；补给只能经拉多加湖运入，夏季靠船运，冬季则经过冰封湖面上的“生命之路”。

sources.title: Anna Reid, Leningrad: The Epic Siege of World War II (2011)
Lidiya Ginzburg, Notes of a Blockade Person (memoir)

note: Civilian death estimates range from about 650,000 to over 1 million.

story.en:
On 8 September 1941 German troops took Shlisselburg on Lake Ladoga and closed the ring around Leningrad, a city of some 2.5 million. Hitler had decided not to storm it but to starve it. The bread ration for dependants fell in November to 125 grams a day, much of it sawdust and cellulose. With no electricity or running water in the coldest winter in years, people burned furniture and books, carried water from holes in the ice of the Neva, and dragged the dead to cemeteries on children's sleds.

In January and February 1942 about 100,000 people died every month. Eleven-year-old Tanya Savicheva recorded the deaths of her family in a small notebook, ending "Everyone died. Only Tanya is left"; she herself died in 1944 after evacuation. Across the frozen Ladoga trucks ran the "Road of Life", carrying food in and evacuees out. In August 1942 Shostakovich's Seventh Symphony was played in the city by a starving orchestra and broadcast at the enemy lines. A land corridor was opened in January 1943, and the siege was fully lifted on 27 January 1944.
story.zh:
1941年9月8日，德军攻占拉多加湖畔的施吕瑟尔堡，完成了对拥有约250万人口的列宁格勒的包围。希特勒决定不强攻，而要把城市饿死。11月，被抚养者的面包配给降至每天125克，其中掺了大量锯末和纤维素。在多年未见的严冬里，城中没有电也没有自来水，人们焚烧家具和书籍取暖，从涅瓦河冰窟里取水，用孩子的雪橇把死者拖到墓地。

1942年1月和2月，每月约有10万人死去。十一岁的塔尼娅·萨维切娃在一个小本子上记下家人相继死去的日子，最后写道：“全都死了。只剩下塔尼娅一个人。”她本人在被疏散后于1944年去世。卡车在冰封的拉多加湖上开辟“生命之路”，运进食物、运出撤离者。1942年8月，一支饥肠辘辘的乐团在城中演奏肖斯塔科维奇的《第七交响曲》，并通过扩音器向敌军阵地播放。1943年1月陆上走廊被打通，1944年1月27日围城彻底解除。

summary.en: When the SS entered the Warsaw Ghetto to deport its remaining Jews to Treblinka, fighters of the Jewish Combat Organisation under Mordechai Anielewicz and the Jewish Military Union resisted with pistols and petrol bombs for almost a month. The Germans burned the ghetto block by block and blew up the Great Synagogue on 16 May.
summary.zh: 党卫队进入华沙犹太区、准备把剩余犹太人遣送至特雷布林卡时，莫迪凯·阿涅莱维奇领导的犹太战斗组织和犹太军事联盟的战士们手持手枪和燃烧瓶抵抗了近一个月。德军逐个街区焚烧犹太区，并于5月16日炸毁大犹太会堂。

sources.title: United States Holocaust Memorial Museum: Warsaw Ghetto Uprising
POLIN Museum of the History of Polish Jews

summary.en: The Polish Home Army rose against the German occupation as the Red Army reached the Vistula, hoping to liberate Warsaw before the Soviets arrived. The Soviets halted, and after 63 days of fighting the insurgents surrendered; some 150,000–200,000 civilians died and the Germans systematically razed the city.
summary.zh: 红军抵达维斯瓦河时，波兰家乡军起而反抗德国占领，希望赶在苏军到来之前解放华沙。苏军却止步不前，经过63天的战斗起义者投降；约15万至20万平民死亡，德军随后有计划地把城市夷为平地。

sources.title: Norman Davies, Rising '44: The Battle for Warsaw (2003)

summary.en: A student demonstration in Budapest turned into a national uprising; crowds toppled Stalin's statue, and Imre Nagy's government announced withdrawal from the Warsaw Pact. On 4 November Soviet tanks crushed the revolution; some 2,500 Hungarians were killed, about 200,000 fled, and Nagy was executed in 1958.
summary.zh: 布达佩斯的一次学生示威演变为全国起义；人群推倒斯大林雕像，纳吉·伊姆雷政府宣布退出华沙条约组织。11月4日苏联坦克镇压了革命，约2500名匈牙利人遇难，约20万人出逃，纳吉于1958年被处决。

sources.title: Charles Gati, Failed Illusions: Moscow, Washington, Budapest, and the 1956 Hungarian Revolt (2006)
Victor Sebestyen, Twelve Days: The Story of the 1956 Hungarian Revolution (2006)

note: polity-kingdom-of-hungary is used as the Hungarian state record; the Hungarian People's Republic has no separate record.

story.en:
Khrushchev's secret speech denouncing Stalin in February 1956 and the Polish crisis that October raised hopes across the Soviet bloc. On 23 October students in Budapest marched in solidarity with Poland and read out sixteen demands, including free elections and the withdrawal of Soviet troops. That evening crowds pulled down the giant bronze Stalin in the City Park, leaving only his boots, and when the state security police fired from the radio building, the protest became an armed uprising.

The reform communist Imre Nagy became prime minister, released prisoners, accepted a multi-party system and on 1 November declared Hungary neutral and out of the Warsaw Pact. For a few days Soviet forces seemed to withdraw. But at dawn on 4 November they returned in overwhelming strength, as the world's attention was divided by the Suez crisis. Young fighters with petrol bombs held out in districts such as Corvin Passage for several days. János Kádár formed a new government; Nagy, lured out of the Yugoslav embassy, was hanged in 1958 and reburied with honours in 1989.
story.zh:
1956年2月赫鲁晓夫谴责斯大林的秘密报告以及同年10月的波兰危机，在整个苏联集团激起了希望。10月23日，布达佩斯学生游行声援波兰，宣读了包括自由选举和苏军撤离在内的十六点要求。当晚，人群在城市公园推倒了巨大的斯大林铜像，只剩下他的一双靴子；国家保安警察从电台大楼开枪后，抗议演变为武装起义。

改革派共产党人纳吉·伊姆雷出任总理，释放政治犯，接受多党制，并于11月1日宣布匈牙利中立、退出华沙条约组织。有几天苏军似乎在撤退。然而11月4日黎明，趁世界的注意力被苏伊士运河危机分散，苏军以压倒性兵力卷土重来。手持燃烧瓶的年轻战士在科尔文巷等街区坚持了数日。卡达尔·亚诺什组成新政府；纳吉被诱出南斯拉夫使馆，1958年被绞死，1989年获隆重重新安葬。

summary.en: Under Alexander Dubček the Czechoslovak Communist Party relaxed censorship and promised "socialism with a human face". On the night of 20–21 August 1968 some 250,000 Warsaw Pact troops invaded, and "normalisation" under Gustáv Husák reversed the reforms. In January 1969 the student Jan Palach burned himself to death in protest.
summary.zh: 在亚历山大·杜布切克领导下，捷克斯洛伐克共产党放松审查，承诺建设“具有人性面孔的社会主义”。1968年8月20日至21日夜，约25万华约军队入侵，古斯塔夫·胡萨克主持的“正常化”推翻了改革。1969年1月，学生扬·帕拉赫自焚抗议。

sources.title: Kieran Williams, The Prague Spring and its Aftermath: Czechoslovak Politics 1968–1970 (1997)
Günter Bischof et al. (eds.), The Prague Spring and the Warsaw Pact Invasion of Czechoslovakia in 1968 (2010)

story.en:
In January 1968 the Slovak communist Alexander Dubček replaced the hard-liner Antonín Novotný as party leader. Within weeks censorship had effectively ended; newspapers investigated the show trials of the 1950s, and in June the writer Ludvík Vaculík's manifesto "Two Thousand Words" urged citizens to push reform from below. The party's Action Programme spoke of freedom of assembly and a federal state, but Dubček insisted that Czechoslovakia would stay in the Warsaw Pact.

Moscow, East Berlin and Warsaw feared contagion. On the night of 20–21 August, Soviet, Polish, Hungarian and Bulgarian troops crossed the border. Czechoslovaks resisted without arms: they turned street signs round, painted slogans and argued with bewildered young soldiers on Wenceslas Square. Dubček was flown to Moscow and forced to sign a protocol accepting occupation. He was removed in April 1969, and through purges and resignations the party lost nearly half a million members. Jan Palach's self-immolation in January 1969 became a symbol that the Velvet Revolution of 1989 would recall.
story.zh:
1968年1月，斯洛伐克共产党人亚历山大·杜布切克取代强硬派安东宁·诺沃提尼出任党的领导人。几周之内审查制度实际上已告终结，报纸开始调查20世纪50年代的公审；6月，作家卢德维克·瓦楚利克发表宣言《两千字》，号召公民自下而上推动改革。党的《行动纲领》谈到集会自由和建立联邦制国家，但杜布切克坚称捷克斯洛伐克仍将留在华沙条约组织内。

莫斯科、东柏林和华沙担心改革会传染开来。8月20日至21日夜，苏联、波兰、匈牙利和保加利亚军队越过边境。捷克斯洛伐克人进行了非武装抵抗：他们把路牌掉转方向，刷写标语，在瓦茨拉夫广场上与茫然的年轻士兵争论。杜布切克被押往莫斯科，被迫签署接受占领的议定书。1969年4月他被撤职，党在清洗和退党中失去了近五十万名党员。1969年1月扬·帕拉赫的自焚成为一个象征，1989年的天鹅绒革命还将重新唤起这段记忆。

summary.en: Strikes at the Lenin Shipyard in Gdańsk led by the electrician Lech Wałęsa won the Gdańsk Agreement, which allowed the first independent trade union in the Soviet bloc. Solidarity grew to about ten million members before martial law in December 1981 drove it underground; round-table talks in 1989 brought it back to win semi-free elections.
summary.zh: 电工莱赫·瓦文萨领导的格但斯克列宁造船厂罢工赢得《格但斯克协议》，苏联集团中第一个独立工会由此诞生。团结工会会员一度达到约一千万，1981年12月实行戒严后被迫转入地下；1989年的圆桌会谈使其重返政坛，并在半自由选举中获胜。

sources.title: Timothy Garton Ash, The Polish Revolution: Solidarity (3rd ed. 2002)

note: Solidarity was formally founded on 17 September 1980; the Gdańsk Agreement was signed on 31 August.

story.en:
In August 1980 the Gdańsk shipyard fired Anna Walentynowicz, a crane operator and veteran activist, five months before her retirement. Her colleagues went on strike, and Lech Wałęsa, an electrician who had himself been dismissed for union activity, climbed over the shipyard fence to lead them. The strike spread along the coast; an inter-factory committee drew up 21 demands, written on plywood boards and hung on the gate, starting with the right to free trade unions.

On 31 August the government gave in, and Wałęsa signed the agreement with an oversized souvenir pen bearing a portrait of the Polish pope John Paul II. Within months Solidarity had around ten million members, a quarter of the population. On 13 December 1981 General Wojciech Jaruzelski declared martial law, arrested thousands of activists and banned the union. It survived underground, Wałęsa won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1983, and in 1989 the communists negotiated with Solidarity at a round table; in the June elections it won all 161 freely contested seats in the Sejm and 99 of the 100 in the new Senate.
story.zh:
1980年8月，格但斯克造船厂在起重机操作员、资深活动家安娜·瓦伦蒂诺维奇退休前五个月将她解雇。她的同事们举行罢工，曾因工会活动被开除的电工莱赫·瓦文萨翻过造船厂围墙前来领导罢工。罢工沿海岸蔓延，厂际罢工委员会起草了21条要求，写在胶合板上挂在厂门口，第一条就是组织自由工会的权利。

8月31日政府让步，瓦文萨用一支印有波兰籍教宗若望·保禄二世画像的超大纪念笔签署了协议。几个月内团结工会会员达到约一千万，占全国人口的四分之一。1981年12月13日，雅鲁泽尔斯基将军宣布戒严，逮捕数千名活动家并取缔工会。团结工会在地下坚持下来，瓦文萨于1983年获诺贝尔和平奖；1989年共产党与团结工会举行圆桌会谈，在6月的选举中，团结工会赢得众议院全部161个自由竞选席位，以及新设参议院100席中的99席。

summary.en: On the 50th anniversary of the Molotov–Ribbentrop Pact, about two million Estonians, Latvians and Lithuanians joined hands in a human chain some 675 km long from Tallinn through Riga to Vilnius, demanding recognition of the secret protocols that had handed their countries to Stalin and the restoration of independence.
summary.zh: 在《莫洛托夫—里宾特洛甫条约》签订五十周年之际，约两百万爱沙尼亚人、拉脱维亚人和立陶宛人手拉手，组成从塔林经里加到维尔纽斯、长约675公里的人链，要求承认把他们的国家交给斯大林的秘密议定书并恢复独立。

sources.title: Britannica: Baltic states: The restoration of independence
UNESCO Memory of the World: The Baltic Way

story.en:
The secret protocols of the Nazi–Soviet pact of 23 August 1939, as revised that September, had assigned Estonia, Latvia and most of Lithuania to the Soviet sphere, and in 1940 they were annexed. For decades Moscow denied that the protocol existed. By 1989 the popular fronts of the three republics, Rahvarinne, the Tautas fronte and Sąjūdis, were openly demanding sovereignty, and they planned a protest on the pact's fiftieth anniversary that would show their unity to the world.

At 7 p.m. on 23 August people from towns and farms along the highway joined hands for fifteen minutes in a chain that ran unbroken, according to the organisers, from Toompea Castle in Tallinn to the Gediminas Tower in Vilnius. Radios coordinated the gaps; flowers and candles were laid; in places the line was several people deep. Moscow denounced the "nationalist hysteria", but in December the Soviet Congress of People's Deputies admitted the protocols. Lithuania declared independence on 11 March 1990, the first Soviet republic to do so.
story.zh:
1939年8月23日纳粹—苏联条约的秘密议定书及同年9月的修订把爱沙尼亚、拉脱维亚和立陶宛大部划入苏联势力范围，1940年三国被吞并。数十年间莫斯科一直否认这份议定书的存在。到1989年，三个加盟共和国的人民阵线——爱沙尼亚人民阵线、拉脱维亚人民阵线和立陶宛的“萨尤季斯”——已公开要求主权，并策划在条约签订五十周年之际举行抗议，向世界展示三国的团结。

8月23日晚7点，公路沿线城镇和农庄的人们手拉手站了十五分钟。据组织者说，人链从塔林的托姆佩亚城堡一直延伸到维尔纽斯的格迪米纳斯塔楼，未曾中断。广播协调填补空缺，人们献上鲜花、点起蜡烛，有些地段人链站了好几排。莫斯科谴责这是“民族主义歇斯底里”，但同年12月苏联人民代表大会承认了秘密议定书的存在。1990年3月11日，立陶宛成为第一个宣布独立的苏联加盟共和国。

summary.en: Riot police beat students at a sanctioned march in Prague on 17 November 1989, sparking daily mass rallies on Wenceslas Square and a general strike. Within six weeks the Communist Party gave up its monopoly of power, and on 29 December the dissident playwright Václav Havel was elected president.
summary.zh: 1989年11月17日，防暴警察殴打布拉格一场经批准游行中的学生，引发瓦茨拉夫广场每日的大规模集会和总罢工。六周之内共产党放弃了权力垄断，12月29日，持不同政见的剧作家瓦茨拉夫·哈维尔当选总统。

sources.title: Timothy Garton Ash, The Magic Lantern: The Revolution of '89 (1990)
James Krapfl, Revolution with a Human Face (2013)

story.en:
On 17 November 1989, fifty years after the Nazis closed Czech universities, students held an officially permitted march in Prague. When thousands turned toward Wenceslas Square, riot police trapped them on Národní Street and beat them; a false rumour that a student had been killed spread through the city. Theatres went on strike and became discussion halls, and on 19 November dissidents led by Václav Havel founded Civic Forum at the Drama Club theatre and soon made the Magic Lantern theatre its headquarters, with Public Against Violence as its Slovak partner.

Night after night hundreds of thousands filled Wenceslas Square, jingling keys to tell the regime its time was up. Alexander Dubček, the hero of 1968, appeared on a balcony beside Havel. A two-hour general strike on 27 November showed that workers too had abandoned the party. The leadership resigned, a government with a non-communist majority was formed, and on 29 December the Federal Assembly, still full of communist deputies, unanimously elected Havel president. Not a single person had died.
story.zh:
1989年11月17日，在纳粹关闭捷克大学五十周年之际，学生们在布拉格举行了一次经官方批准的游行。当数千人转向瓦茨拉夫广场时，防暴警察把他们堵在民族大街上殴打；一个学生被打死的谣言（后证实不实）传遍全城。剧院纷纷罢演，变成讨论会场；11月19日，以瓦茨拉夫·哈维尔为首的异见人士在“话剧俱乐部”剧院成立“公民论坛”，随后以“魔灯”剧院为总部，斯洛伐克方面则成立了“公众反暴力”。

一夜又一夜，数十万人挤满瓦茨拉夫广场，摇响手中的钥匙，告诉政权它的时间到了。1968年的英雄亚历山大·杜布切克与哈维尔一同出现在阳台上。11月27日的两小时总罢工表明工人也已抛弃了共产党。领导层辞职，组成了非共产党人占多数的政府；12月29日，仍由共产党议员占多数的联邦议会一致选举哈维尔为总统。整个过程中没有一个人死亡。

summary.en: Three days after the failed August coup in Moscow, the Verkhovna Rada of the Ukrainian SSR declared Ukraine independent. In a referendum on 1 December 1991 over 90 percent of voters, including a majority in every region and in Crimea, approved, and Leonid Kravchuk was elected president; a week later the Belovezha Accords dissolved the USSR.
summary.zh: 莫斯科“八一九”政变失败三天后，乌克兰苏维埃社会主义共和国最高拉达宣布乌克兰独立。1991年12月1日的全民公决中，超过90%的选民——包括每个地区和克里米亚的多数选民——投票赞成，列昂尼德·克拉夫丘克当选总统；一周后《别洛韦日协定》宣告苏联解体。

sources.title: Serhii Plokhy, The Last Empire: The Final Days of the Soviet Union (2014)
Serhy Yekelchyk, Ukraine: Birth of a Modern Nation (2007)

story.en:
On 19 August 1991 hard-liners in Moscow placed Gorbachev under house arrest in the Crimea and declared a state of emergency. The coup collapsed within three days, and with it the authority of the Soviet centre. In Kyiv the communist majority of the Verkhovna Rada, led by its chairman Leonid Kravchuk, now saw independence as the safest course; on 24 August the parliament voted 346 to 1 for the Act of Declaration of Independence, to be confirmed by referendum.

The vote on 1 December surprised many observers: about 84 percent of the electorate turned out and over 90 percent said yes, including majorities in Russian-speaking Donetsk and Crimea. Kravchuk was elected president the same day. George H. W. Bush had warned Ukrainians against "suicidal nationalism" in Kyiv that summer, but without Ukraine Boris Yeltsin saw no future for a union treaty. A week later Kravchuk, Yeltsin and the Belarusian leader Stanislav Shushkevich met in the Belovezha forest and declared that the USSR had ceased to exist.
story.zh:
1991年8月19日，莫斯科的强硬派将在克里米亚度假的戈尔巴乔夫软禁，宣布进入紧急状态。政变三天内即告失败，苏联中央的权威也随之瓦解。在基辅，以议长列昂尼德·克拉夫丘克为首、共产党人占多数的最高拉达此时认为独立是最稳妥的选择；8月24日，议会以346票对1票通过《乌克兰独立宣言》，并决定交付全民公决确认。

12月1日的投票结果出乎许多观察家意料：约84%的选民参加投票，其中超过90%投了赞成票，讲俄语为主的顿涅茨克和克里米亚也是多数赞成。克拉夫丘克同日当选总统。那年夏天，老布什总统曾在基辅告诫乌克兰人不要搞“自杀性的民族主义”，但没有乌克兰，叶利钦认为新联盟条约已无前途。一周后，克拉夫丘克、叶利钦和白俄罗斯领导人舒什克维奇在别洛韦日森林会晤，宣布苏联不复存在。

name.zh: 捷克斯洛伐克解体（“天鹅绒分离”）

summary.en: After the 1992 elections the Czech and Slovak leaders, Václav Klaus and Vladimír Mečiar, could not agree on the shape of the federation and negotiated a peaceful split without a referendum. On 1 January 1993 the Czech Republic and Slovakia became independent states.
summary.zh: 1992年大选后，捷克和斯洛伐克的领导人瓦茨拉夫·克劳斯与弗拉基米尔·梅恰尔无法就联邦形式达成一致，在未举行全民公决的情况下协商和平分家。1993年1月1日，捷克共和国和斯洛伐克成为独立国家。

sources.title: Abby Innes, Czechoslovakia: The Short Goodbye (2001)

summary.en: During the Bosnian War, Bosnian Serb forces under Ratko Mladić overran the UN-declared "safe area" of Srebrenica, guarded by lightly armed Dutch peacekeepers, and killed more than 8,000 Bosniak men and boys. International courts have ruled it a genocide; Mladić and Radovan Karadžić were convicted.
summary.zh: 波黑战争期间，拉特科·姆拉迪奇指挥的波斯尼亚塞族武装攻占由轻装荷兰维和部队守卫的联合国“安全区”斯雷布雷尼察，杀害了八千多名波什尼亚克族男子和男孩。国际法院和前南刑庭裁定其为种族灭绝；姆拉迪奇和拉多万·卡拉季奇已被定罪。

sources.title: International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia: Srebrenica
International Court of Justice, Bosnia and Herzegovina v. Serbia and Montenegro, judgment of 26 February 2007

note: Linked to polity-yugoslavia for the wars of the Yugoslav succession, though the SFRY had dissolved by 1992.

story.en:
The wars that broke up Yugoslavia began in Slovenia and Croatia in 1991 and reached Bosnia and Herzegovina in 1992. Srebrenica, a mining town in the Drina valley, filled with Bosniak refugees as Bosnian Serb forces cleared surrounding villages, and in 1993 the UN Security Council declared it a "safe area". In July 1995 the Army of Republika Srpska under General Ratko Mladić attacked. The small Dutch battalion's requests for NATO air support produced only limited strikes, and on 11 July Mladić walked into the town before television cameras.

Thousands of women, children and elderly people were bussed out. The men and boys were separated, or caught in the woods as a column of about 15,000 tried to break through to Bosnian government territory. Over the following days they were shot at sites such as Kravica, Orahovac and Branjevo; the bodies were later dug up by machines and scattered in secondary graves to hide the crime. DNA analysis has since identified most of more than 8,000 victims, and 11 July is marked as a day of remembrance.
story.zh:
南斯拉夫解体战争1991年始于斯洛文尼亚和克罗地亚，1992年蔓延到波斯尼亚和黑塞哥维那。随着波斯尼亚塞族武装清洗周边村庄，德里纳河谷的矿业小城斯雷布雷尼察挤满了波什尼亚克族难民；1993年联合国安理会宣布其为“安全区”。1995年7月，拉特科·姆拉迪奇将军指挥的塞族共和国军发起进攻。小股荷兰营请求北约空中支援，换来的只是有限的打击；7月11日，姆拉迪奇在电视镜头前走进城中。

数以千计的妇女、儿童和老人被大巴运走。男子和男孩或被单独分离，或在约1.5万人的队伍试图突围前往波黑政府控制区时在树林中被抓获。此后数日，他们在克拉维察、奥拉霍瓦茨、布拉涅沃等地被枪杀；为掩盖罪行，尸体后来又被机械挖出，分散埋入二次墓穴。此后的DNA鉴定已确认了八千多名遇难者中的大多数，7月11日成为纪念日。

summary.en: Ten countries joined the European Union on 1 May 2004: Poland, Czechia, Slovakia, Hungary, Slovenia, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Cyprus and Malta. Most had joined NATO in 1999 or 2004; Bulgaria and Romania followed in 2007 and Croatia in 2013, completing the post-communist "return to Europe".
summary.zh: 2004年5月1日，波兰、捷克、斯洛伐克、匈牙利、斯洛文尼亚、爱沙尼亚、拉脱维亚、立陶宛、塞浦路斯和马耳他十国加入欧盟。其中大多数已在1999年或2004年加入北约；保加利亚和罗马尼亚于2007年、克罗地亚于2013年相继入盟，完成了后共产主义国家的“回归欧洲”。

note: Plotted at Kraków as a representative point of the accession states.

name.en: Euromaidan and the Revolution of Dignity

summary.en: Protests began on Kyiv's Maidan Nezalezhnosti in November 2013 after President Viktor Yanukovych dropped an association agreement with the EU. After the violent dispersal of students and a winter-long occupation, police and snipers killed about 100 protesters in February 2014; Yanukovych fled to Russia and parliament removed him.
summary.zh: 2013年11月，总统维克托·亚努科维奇放弃与欧盟的联系国协定，抗议随即在基辅独立广场爆发。学生遭暴力驱散后，抗议者占领广场整整一个冬天；2014年2月，警察和狙击手打死约一百名抗议者，亚努科维奇逃往俄罗斯，议会解除了他的职务。

sources.title: Andrew Wilson, Ukraine Crisis: What It Means for the West (2014)
Serhii Plokhy, The Gates of Europe: A History of Ukraine (rev. ed. 2021)

summary.en: After the fall of Yanukovych, Russian soldiers without insignia seized Crimea's parliament and key sites. A referendum held under occupation and not recognised internationally was followed by annexation on 18 March 2014. The UN General Assembly affirmed Ukraine's territorial integrity, and fighting soon began in the Donbas.
summary.zh: 亚努科维奇倒台后，不佩戴标识的俄罗斯军人占领克里米亚议会和要地。在占领状态下举行、未获国际承认的公投之后，俄罗斯于2014年3月18日宣布吞并克里米亚。联合国大会决议重申乌克兰的领土完整，顿巴斯地区不久也爆发战事。

sources.title: UN General Assembly resolution 68/262, "Territorial integrity of Ukraine" (27 March 2014)

name.zh: 俄罗斯全面入侵乌克兰

summary.en: On 24 February 2022 Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine from the north, east and south. Ukraine stopped the drive on Kyiv and in autumn 2022 retook much of Kharkiv region and the city of Kherson; the war then became a slow war of attrition in the east and south. By late 2025 the UN had verified some 14,500 civilian deaths, and millions had fled.
summary.zh: 2022年2月24日，俄罗斯从北、东、南三个方向全面入侵乌克兰。乌克兰挫败了对基辅的进攻，并于2022年秋收复哈尔科夫州大部和赫尔松市；此后战争在东部和南部演变为缓慢的消耗战。截至2025年末，联合国已核实约1.45万名平民死亡，数百万人逃离家园。

label.en: Fighting at Bucha, Irpin and Hostomel; drive on Kyiv halted
label.zh: 布恰、伊尔平和霍斯托梅尔之战，对基辅的进攻受挫
马里乌波尔之围
哈尔科夫反攻
赫尔松光复
巴赫穆特战役
俄军向波克罗夫斯克推进

sources.title: UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine: Protection of Civilians in Armed Conflict, monthly updates (2025)
Serhii Plokhy, The Russo-Ukrainian War: The Return of History (2023)
UN General Assembly resolution ES-11/4, "Territorial integrity of Ukraine: defending the principles of the Charter" (12 October 2022)

note: Ongoing war; casualty figures are contested and change over time. The UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission had verified about 14,500 civilian deaths and over 53,000 civilian casualties by the end of October 2025 and states the real toll is considerably higher; neither side publishes reliable military losses. endYear 2025 marks the end of the atlas timeline, not the end of the war.

story.en:
After months of military build-up, Vladimir Putin announced a "special military operation" before dawn on 24 February 2022, saying its aims were the "demilitarisation and denazification" of Ukraine, claims rejected by Ukraine, the UN General Assembly majority and most governments. Columns advanced on Kyiv from Belarus, airborne troops landed at Hostomel airport, and Russian forces seized much of the south, including Kherson. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stayed in Kyiv, and the government did not fall.

By early April the Russians had withdrawn from around the capital; in Bucha and other towns investigators documented killings of civilians. Mariupol fell in May after a siege that destroyed most of the city. In September 2022 Russia proclaimed the annexation of four Ukrainian regions, a step the UN General Assembly declared invalid, while Ukraine, armed by Western states, retook much of Kharkiv region and then Kherson. A Ukrainian counteroffensive in 2023 gained little ground, and the war became one of trenches, artillery and drones, with Russian forces advancing slowly in the Donbas through 2024 and 2025. Talks in Istanbul and US-led diplomacy in 2025 brought prisoner exchanges but no ceasefire by the end of the year.
story.zh:
经过数月军事集结，弗拉基米尔·普京于2022年2月24日凌晨宣布发动“特别军事行动”，声称目的是使乌克兰“非军事化和去纳粹化”，这一说法遭到乌克兰、联合国大会多数成员国和大多数国家政府的驳斥。俄军纵队从白俄罗斯向基辅推进，空降兵在霍斯托梅尔机场着陆，南方的赫尔松等大片地区被俄军占领。泽连斯基总统留守基辅，政府没有垮台。

到4月初，俄军已从首都周边撤退；调查人员在布恰等城镇记录了杀害平民的事件。马里乌波尔在长期围困中大部被毁，于5月陷落。2022年9月，俄罗斯宣布吞并乌克兰四个州，联合国大会宣布此举无效；获得西方武器援助的乌克兰则收复哈尔科夫州大部，随后收复赫尔松。2023年乌克兰的反攻进展甚微，战争变成了堑壕、炮兵与无人机的较量，2024年至2025年俄军在顿巴斯缓慢推进。2025年在伊斯坦布尔举行的谈判和美国主导的外交斡旋促成了交换战俘，但到年底仍未实现停火。

summary.en: Germanic and Sarmatian peoples led by the Marcomanni and Quadi crossed the middle Danube and even reached Aquileia in Italy. Marcus Aurelius spent most of his last years campaigning from bases such as Carnuntum, writing parts of his Meditations in camp, and died at the front in 180; his son Commodus made peace.
summary.zh: 以马科曼尼人和夸德人为首的日耳曼和萨尔马提亚诸族越过多瑙河中游，甚至攻至意大利的阿奎莱亚。马可·奥勒留晚年大部分时间以卡农图姆等基地为大本营作战，在军营中写下《沉思录》的部分篇章，180年死于前线；其子康茂德随后议和。

sources.title: Anthony R. Birley, Marcus Aurelius: A Biography (rev. ed. 2000)

note: Plotted at Carnuntum, the main Roman base on the middle Danube (opposite modern Bratislava).

summary.en: Goths under Cniva, who had sacked Philippopolis, trapped the Roman army in marshy ground near Abritus in Moesia. Emperor Decius and his son Herennius Etruscus were killed, the first Roman emperor to die fighting a foreign enemy, at the height of the third-century crisis.
summary.zh: 刚刚洗劫腓力波利斯的哥特首领克尼瓦，在默西亚的阿布里图斯附近把罗马军队困于沼泽地带。德西乌斯皇帝及其子赫伦尼乌斯·伊特鲁斯库斯阵亡，他是第一位死于对外战争的罗马皇帝，时值三世纪危机的高峰。

note: Located at Abritus (modern Razgrad, Bulgaria); linked to Philippopolis (Plovdiv), sacked in the same campaign.

summary.en: Dying of a painful illness, Emperor Galerius, a chief instigator of the Great Persecution, issued an edict at Serdica (Sofia) ending the persecution of Christians in the East and allowing them to worship and rebuild their churches, two years before the Edict of Milan.
summary.zh: 身患重病、行将就木的伽列里乌斯皇帝——大迫害的主要发动者之一——在塞尔迪卡（今索非亚）颁布敕令，结束东部对基督徒的迫害，准许他们礼拜和重建教堂，比《米兰敕令》早两年。

sources.title: Lactantius, On the Deaths of the Persecutors 33–35

summary.en: Tsar Simeon I of Bulgaria routed a large Byzantine army under Leo Phokas near the Achelous river on the Black Sea coast, one of the bloodiest battles of the Middle Ages. The victory left Simeon master of the Balkans, though he never captured Constantinople.
summary.zh: 保加利亚沙皇西美昂一世在黑海沿岸的阿谢洛奥斯河附近击溃利奥·福卡斯统率的拜占庭大军，这是中世纪最血腥的战役之一。此役使西美昂称雄巴尔干，但他始终未能攻下君士坦丁堡。

sources.title: John Skylitzes, Synopsis of Histories, reign of Constantine VII

summary.en: A coalition of eleven princes sent by Andrey Bogolyubsky of Vladimir-Suzdal stormed and plundered Kyiv for two days. Andrey did not move to Kyiv but gave it to his brother, a sign that the centre of power in Rus' had shifted to the north-east.
summary.zh: 弗拉基米尔—苏兹达尔的安德烈·博戈柳布斯基派出的十一位王公联军攻破基辅，劫掠两日。安德烈并未迁居基辅，而是把它交给弟弟，表明罗斯的权力中心已转移到东北。

sources.title: Simon Franklin & Jonathan Shepard, The Emergence of Rus 750–1200 (1996)

summary.en: Angered by new taxes levied for Isaac II's wedding, the brothers Theodore-Peter and Ivan Asen raised the Bulgarians and Vlachs north of the Balkan range. Proclaiming independence at Tarnovo, they founded the Second Bulgarian Empire, which Byzantium recognised in 1187.
summary.zh: 因不满伊萨克二世为婚礼加征新税，西奥多—彼得与伊凡·阿森兄弟在巴尔干山以北发动保加利亚人和弗拉赫人起义。他们在特尔诺沃宣布独立，建立第二保加利亚帝国，拜占庭于1187年予以承认。

sources.title: Niketas Choniates, Historia (O City of Byzantium)
Britannica: Bulgaria: The Second Bulgarian Empire

note: The revolt began in late 1185 or 1186.

summary.en: Emperor Theodosius II had a commission gather the general laws issued by Christian emperors since Constantine into sixteen books, promulgated at Constantinople in February 438 and in force from 1 January 439 in both halves of the empire. It is the main surviving source for late Roman law and shaped the law codes of the Germanic kingdoms.
summary.zh: 皇帝狄奥多西二世命委员会把君士坦丁以来历代基督教皇帝颁布的通行法令汇编成十六卷，于438年2月在君士坦丁堡颁布，自439年1月1日起在帝国东西两部同时生效。它是现存晚期罗马法的主要史料，并影响了日耳曼诸王国的法典。

sources.title: Jill Harries & Ian Wood (eds.), The Theodosian Code: Studies in the Imperial Law of Late Antiquity (1993)
Clyde Pharr (trans.), The Theodosian Code and Novels and the Sirmondian Constitutions (1952)

summary.en: A year after Attila's death, the Gepids under King Ardaric and other subject peoples rose against his sons and defeated the Huns at the Nedao river in Pannonia; Attila's eldest son Ellac was killed. The Hunnic empire broke apart, the Gepids took the lands east of the Tisza, and the Goths settled in Pannonia as Roman federates.
summary.zh: 阿提拉死后一年，格皮德国王阿尔达里克率领格皮德人和其他臣属民族起兵反抗阿提拉诸子，在潘诺尼亚的尼达欧河击败匈人，阿提拉的长子埃拉克阵亡。匈人帝国随之瓦解，格皮德人占据蒂萨河以东地区，哥特人则作为罗马的同盟者定居潘诺尼亚。

sources.title: Peter Heather, The Fall of the Roman Empire: A New History (2005)

note: Jordanes is the only detailed source; the river Nedao has not been identified (it was somewhere in Pannonia, perhaps a tributary of the Sava) and the year may be 454 or 455. The point follows Wikidata and is approximate; the part played by the Ostrogoths is disputed.

summary.en: Prince Sviatoslav I of Kiev, who had overrun Bulgaria in 968–969, was besieged at Dorostolon (Silistra) on the Danube by Emperor John I Tzimiskes from April to July 971. After failed sorties he agreed to leave the Balkans; Pechenegs killed him on his way home, and Byzantium annexed eastern Bulgaria.
summary.zh: 968—969年横扫保加利亚的基辅大公斯维亚托斯拉夫一世，于971年4月至7月被拜占庭皇帝约翰一世·齐米斯基斯围困在多瑙河畔的多罗斯托隆（今锡利斯特拉）。几次突围失败后，他同意撤离巴尔干；归途中他被佩切涅格人杀死，拜占庭则吞并了保加利亚东部。

story.en:
Sviatoslav came to the Balkans at Byzantium's invitation: in 968 Emperor Nikephoros II paid him to attack the Bulgarians. He did so with such success that, according to the Primary Chronicle, he wanted to make Pereyaslavets on the Danube the centre of his lands. In 970 his army pushed into Thrace, and the new emperor, John Tzimiskes, decided to drive him out.

In April 971 Tzimiskes stormed Preslav and captured the Bulgarian tsar Boris II, then shut Sviatoslav inside Dorostolon, with a fleet carrying Greek fire on the river. For about three months the Rus' fought sorties outside the walls. Leo the Deacon, who knew eyewitnesses, describes the prince coming to the riverbank to negotiate: rowing with his men, in a plain white shirt, his head shaved except for one lock, a single gold earring in one ear. He promised to leave Bulgaria in return for safe passage and grain. On the way home in 972 the Pechenegs ambushed him at the Dnieper rapids, and the chronicle says their khan Kurya made a drinking cup of his skull.
story.zh:
斯维亚托斯拉夫是应拜占庭之邀来到巴尔干的：968年，皇帝尼基弗鲁斯二世出钱请他进攻保加利亚人。他大获全胜，据《往年纪事》记载，他甚至想把多瑙河畔的佩列亚斯拉韦茨作为自己领地的中心。970年他的军队攻入色雷斯，新皇帝约翰·齐米斯基斯决心将他逐出。

971年4月，齐米斯基斯攻下普雷斯拉夫，俘虏保加利亚沙皇鲍里斯二世，随后把斯维亚托斯拉夫围困在多罗斯托隆城内，并派载有希腊火的舰队封锁多瑙河。罗斯人在城外反复出击，坚持了约三个月。曾向目击者打听过情况的执事利奥描写了这位王公来到河岸谈判的情形：他与部下一同划桨，身穿朴素的白衣，头发剃光只留一绺，一只耳朵戴着一枚金耳环。他答应撤出保加利亚，以换取安全返回和粮食。972年归途中，佩切涅格人在第聂伯河险滩伏击了他，编年史称其可汗库里亚用他的头骨做了酒杯。

sources.title: Leo the Deacon, History, books VIII–IX (trans. A.-M. Talbot & D. F. Sullivan, 2005)
The Russian Primary Chronicle, entries for 6479–6480 (971–972)

summary.en: When Pecheneg nomads crossed the Danube and raided Thrace, Emperor John II Komnenos met them near Beroia (Stara Zagora). The Varangian Guard broke into their circle of wagons, and the defeat ended the Pechenegs as an independent people; John founded a festival to mark the victory.
summary.zh: 佩切涅格游牧民越过多瑙河劫掠色雷斯，拜占庭皇帝约翰二世·科穆宁在贝罗亚（今斯塔拉扎戈拉）附近迎战。瓦良格卫队冲破了他们的车阵，此战之后佩切涅格人不再作为独立民族存在；约翰还设立节庆纪念这场胜利。

sources.title: John Kinnamos, Deeds of John and Manuel Comnenus I.3
Niketas Choniates, Historia (O City of Byzantium), reign of John II

note: Choniates and Kinnamos do not give a firm year; 1122 is the usual date, though 1119–1121 have been proposed.

summary.en: Under 1147 the Hypatian Chronicle records that Prince Yuri Dolgoruky of Suzdal invited his ally Sviatoslav Olgovich: "Come to me, brother, to Moskov", and gave him a great feast there. This is the earliest written mention of Moscow; Yuri fortified the settlement with a wooden wall in 1156.
summary.zh: 《伊帕季耶夫编年史》1147年条记载，苏兹达尔王公尤里·多尔戈鲁基邀请盟友斯维亚托斯拉夫·奥尔戈维奇：“兄弟，到莫斯科来见我吧”，并在那里设下盛宴款待。这是莫斯科最早的文字记载；1156年尤里为该地筑起木墙。

note: No Wikidata item exists for the first mention itself. Archaeology shows the site was settled before 1147; the chronicle entry is the conventional founding date, celebrated in the 850th anniversary of 1997.

summary.en: A Byzantine army under Andronikos Kontostephanos, sent by Emperor Manuel I Komnenos, routed the Hungarian army of King Stephen III near Sirmium on the Sava. The peace that followed confirmed Byzantine rule over Sirmium, Bosnia and Dalmatia, the high point of Manuel's power in the Balkans.
summary.zh: 拜占庭皇帝曼努埃尔一世·科穆宁派安德罗尼卡·康托斯特法诺斯率军，在萨瓦河畔的锡尔米乌姆附近击溃匈牙利国王斯蒂芬三世的军队。随后的和约确认拜占庭对锡尔米乌姆、波斯尼亚和达尔马提亚的统治，这是曼努埃尔在巴尔干权势的顶峰。

sources.title: John Kinnamos, Deeds of John and Manuel Comnenus VI.7
Niketas Choniates, Historia (O City of Byzantium), reign of Manuel I
Paul Magdalino, The Empire of Manuel I Komnenos, 1143–1180 (1993)
